Joycraft adversarial panel · Claude side · Fable 5.1 at high effort · 2026-09-24

Dynamic Joycraft: what survived the panel

Twelve propositions about reimagining Joycraft as a dynamic harness, each attacked by three to five lensed skeptics and ruled on by a judge, then synthesized. Every skeptic re-checked citations against live sources. Read the synthesis first, then the rulings you care about. The Codex panel runs separately; compare both before deciding anything.

Synthesis

What the panel recommends

Summary

Twelve rulings: ten qualify, two flip (P6 Jev-on-hot-path, P11 user-background fork), zero keep. The panel converged from seven lenses on one verdict: the "dynamic" half of the reimagining (agent-generated process prose, Jev routing, runtime-fetched guidance, marketplace plugin, per-user fork) has null-to-negative primary evidence and every verified pain maps to an existing code path plus one missing gate. What survives is a subtraction-and-consolidation program on the current architecture delivered as an ordinary versioned update, plus three bounded new things: (1) a blocking shippability gate at the in-review→done and merge boundary with joycraft-verify actually wired, (2) a vendored manifest-pinned state oracle for all five harnesses, (3) a new idempotent AGENTS.md marker-patch kind so anything reaches the ~15 existing installs. The maintainer's Q4 diagnosis (hours of unshippable output, close the gap) is the only motive the incremental list does not cover, and it has zero written record; the recommended cure moves from hooks to the status/merge boundary because no host sells a non-overridable hook, Joycraft's one blocking hook was a silent no-op for six months, and branch protection on main has zero required checks. The lead's synthesis (section 9) was right on direction for 5 of 7 threads and wrong on mechanism for most of them: hub skill, forwarding shims, npx CLI oracle, fetch profiles, marketplace plugin, panels-as-standard, and prose generation all lose; router block, disable-model-invocation, subtract audit, two skill dirs, no-MCP, and Jev-advisory-first all hold. Five of the maintainer's own positions moved (Q1 generated prose, Q2 transfer claim, Q3 fetch mechanism, Q4 cure, Q5 Jev core); the invariant half of Q1 and the Q4 goal sentence did not.

First build

The shippability boundary at in-review→done, in four moves that need no failure analysis to be correct because they are check-agnostic: (1) today, zero code — turn on required status checks on main (tests + typecheck + STE lint; gh api shows required_checks: [] and enforce_admins: false, so the 'merge boundary outside the agent's process' the panel leans on does not exist yet); (2) an exit-code test step in .pi/scripts/joycraft/joycraft-implement-loop between implement and spec-done (lines 79-88 run none); (3) a validation precondition on joycraft-mark-done --to done; (4) wire joycraft-verify as the in-review→done transition (zero inbound references today; session-end.md:138 'Once verify-in-loop ships … until then, this step does'), reading an oracle the implementing agent did not author. Each gate ships with a stdin-fixture contract test that drives it exactly as the host does, and hooks stay pre-filter. This is the one verified gap the incremental list does not close and it is what Q4 asks for; it is preceded by the first measurement below and must be reconciled with D2 before any Stop-hook design. The second build, immediately after, is the marker-patch ownership kind generalizing update-inventory.ts:561-592, because the router block and folder-map repair reach nobody's existing install without it.

First measure

Write down the slop. A failure analysis of the recent green-but-unshippable implement-loop sessions in docs/discoveries — which harness and model, which spec, whether tests ran, whether typecheck/STE lint ran, whether session-end's validation step was reached, whether verify was ever invoked, and whether the defect was mechanical (checkable) or semantic (green tests, wrong behaviour). Today grep for slop/unshippable across docs/discoveries, docs/context, docs/backlog, docs/intent returns only STE prose-rule rows and the intent's one-line assertion; P0, P3, P4, and P9 all hinge on a fact with zero written record, and the choice between deterministic checks and an independent verifier as the primary vehicle cannot be made without it. Paired second measurement, cheap and parallel: extend src/telemetry.ts to count Skill tool_use events (already recognized at line 114) across the ~15 colleague installs, so 'users forget the slash commands' and any Jev shadow-mode comparison have a baseline; then a claude plugin eval skill-trigger set with a no-plugin arm.

Recommended shape

  1. Consolidate as one ordinary versioned update, not a rewrite: publish one harness-neutral skills tree to .agents/skills + .claude/skills only (retire .pi/skills, .github/skills, .omp/skills after verifying Pi's runtime actually reads project-level .agents/skills and that Copilot/Cursor/omp dedupe same-named skills); set disable-model-invocation: true on the 11 entry: agent skills for Claude and emit agents/openai.yaml with policy.allow_implicit_invocation: false for Codex (frontmatter flag ignored there, openai/codex#29989); rewrite the 9 human-door descriptions in users' words (today only joycraft-setup speaks in them). No hub skill yet; no permanent forwarding shims (Superpowers deleted exactly that for confusing the model, #756; BMAD's went opt-in in 25 days). Delete joycraft-setup's pure-forwarder body or fold it into the router.
  2. Build a new idempotent marker-patch ownership path that generalizes contextMapPointerPatch (src/update-inventory.ts:561-592) to two targets: a compact always-loaded router block in AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md (the only discoverability fix with a measured 100%, Vercel 2026-01-27), and the folder-map sentinel promoted from create-once to a regenerable owned region (fixes joycraft-tune.md:63's broken 'upgrade regenerates it' promise; this repo's AGENTS.md has zero docs/intent rows while the folder exists). Without this kind, materializeDocuments (update-inventory.ts:236-262) means nothing new ever reaches the 15 colleagues' installs.
  3. Shippability invariant at the boundary the agent cannot reach, in this order: (a) flip required status checks on main to tests + typecheck + STE lint (today required_checks: [], enforce_admins: false; zero code); (b) add an exit-code test step to .pi/scripts/joycraft/joycraft-implement-loop between implement and spec-done (lines 79-88 run none today); (c) give joycraft-mark-done --to done a validation precondition (today accepts any state name); (d) wire joycraft-verify as the in-review→done transition it was designed for (zero inbound references; session-end.md:138 still says 'Once verify-in-loop ships'), reading an oracle the implementing agent did not author (locked tests, CI on branch). Vendor hooks are pre-filter only: PreToolUse fails open on timeout (Claude Code verbatim, Codex by inference), Stop caps at 8 consecutive blocks, .claude/settings.json is not on the deny list. Every gate ships with a stdin-fixture contract test that drives it as the host does (the block-dangerous.sh argv lesson) and runs warn-only until fire/false-positive rate is measured. Add Edit(.claude/settings.json) to the deny list. Reconcile with D2 (2026-09-23, 'No continuation logic and no Stop-hook recipe') before designing any completion gate.
  4. State oracle as a vendored, dependency-free node script in docs/.joycraft/ (the check.mjs pattern), hashed in the manifest at the skills' vendorVersion, installed for all five harnesses (today PI_SCRIPTS are pi-only, bundle-inventory.ts:177; the omp implement variant says 'edit the JSON directly'), emitting versioned --json, never a silent success ({ok:false, reason} on stdout with exit 0 so Claude Code's !command does not abort the skill), sole writer of spec status (own both queue JSON and frontmatter or drop frontmatter status), replacing the five Pi bash scripts (~430 lines) and the prose copy of the next-spec rule in implement.md/implement-feature.md so exactly one definition exists. Scope: queue, status, next, and the computable briefing lines (Start, Order, Decisions stamped, Execution, Done-when). Never npx joycraft <cmd> at skill runtime (0.7.6 and 0.7.10 were both stale-npx releases). Fixture tests for compact and pretty-printed manifests. Restate the promise: it shrinks the pasted briefing to its judgment lines; it does not remove /clear, which the skills justify as context hygiene (bugfix.md:265, new-feature.md:514). Use context: fork on Claude and pi -p on Pi for that; Codex/Copilot/omp keep the human as glue.
  5. Prose cut = ceremony and duplication first, protocol only behind an eval. Cut now without measurement: the ~45-60 line HTML render block repeated in 7 skills, 'Recommended Next Steps' menus, 'Why:' narration (Claude Code docs: 'state what to do rather than narrating how or why'), and the three research/verify harness bodies that differ only by subagent mechanics. Trim new-feature (509 installed, over Claude Code's 500-line limit) and decompose (436). Do NOT cut: verify (176 installed; ~60% is the oracle step, verifier prompt, and report contract — the thing P8 says to keep), research's brief-isolation rule, capped Step 0 retrieval, and Phase 4 reconciliation, or new-feature's human-facing question discipline (forced choice, >=2 real options, defer-to-name, ten-line cap; the repo's own 2026-07-29 note says pointers get skipped, keep it inline). Any protocol cut ships behind a with/without eval (claude plugin eval or pi -p equivalent) on every model class the one path serves, including one open-weight Pi config — AGENTS.md dispatches Pi on kimi-k3, and the Pi tree is already the shortest.
  6. Design-bookend timing fix, subtractive only: one sentence in the shared question directive of the eight gate skills — while the human says they are still exploring, stay in chat and render no checkpoint; the human declares clarity, the agent never infers it. Add a fourth escape (__explore) to CHECKPOINT_TEMPLATE.html and interactive-checkpoint.md that leaves the question `open` with an owner (default the answerer) and a revisit gate, returns to chat, never auto-routes to a panel. Adjudicate the Deposition Checkpoint pilot's kill criterion on the record (count bypasses since 2026-07-20; stamp 'bypass while exploring is expected; bypass once declared clear kills the format'). Visuals inline in existing design.html/review-gate/checkpoint renders under D1's one-template rule — mockups for frontend first, sequence/data-flow diagrams only when the existing human-approved risk judgment marks the feature complex. Panels stay hand-run and human-decided (zero skill mechanism, zero cost figures across 3/13/52/~50-agent runs, Helix has no pre-code panel step, the fully front-loaded Opus 5.5 feature was parked the day it was approved). No new diagram/prototype templates until the non-Claude checkpoint server ships (today paste-back on four harnesses = RF-KILL-6).
  7. Model profiles: keep the curated, condensed, dated per-model profile as the delivered artifact (already kind: vendor, docs/.joycraft/manifest.json:951-955, replaced on every update, auto-released on merge). Unpark the two specs from feature/opus-5-5-prompting that are the subtract half and the delivery half: spec 8 (flag-thinking-rules-in-optimize, extends Step 2c's MODEL_SUPERSEDED audit) and spec 3 (swap-profile-row-on-update). Key profile installation to the running model read from harness config, not to the harness (src/model-profile.ts:20 ships Fable steering to a Pi run on kimi-k3); open-weight/unknown models get no Claude profile. Fetch only as a repo-local maintainer skill under src/local-skills/ that diffs the vendor .md against the profile via llms.txt discovery with redirects followed and drafts a subtract list; the CLI never fetches; no new ownership kind. Restore the load-bearing sentence hand condensation dropped ('The user is not watching in real time', absent from profile:39-43). First new block lands only behind a with/without run that tests whether the profile does anything inside Claude Code at all.
  8. Distribution: CLI remains the sole carrier of CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md, hooks, settings patches, templates, check.mjs, and Pi runtime files, and the update channel for every harness. 'Claude plugin' means only a project-scope skills-directory plugin — a .claude-plugin/plugin.json the CLI writes and git commits inside .claude/skills/, loaded as joycraft@skills-dir (verified: 'reaches every collaborator who clones it'), used for claude plugin eval in CI; no marketplace, no second version string, no second release step; strike 'install hints' (official-marketplace only). Marketplace plugin deferred until skills are stable one quarter and either claude-plugins-official lists Joycraft or the manifest gains a plugin-version kind. 'One tree' requires harness-neutral bodies: 141 {{skill_prefix}}, 21 {{clear}}, 13 {{skills_dir}} sites plus body forks in implement-feature/research/verify/lockdown move to a per-harness header or the AGENTS.md router line. No MCP main channel (no condition needed).
  9. Jev: opt-in, bring-your-own-key, off by default, off the hot path first — doc ranking and report-claim verification over code-filtered state (jev-1.13's own guidance: 'Retrieve and filter in code first'). Second, a shadow-mode skill router that logs Jev's pick beside the skill actually used across the ~15 installs. Hot-path routing only after a held-out eval on Joycraft's own roster with real prompts from telemetry (not prompts authored from the skills' descriptions) beats disable-model-invocation + a model-free forced-eval router block (22/22, 0/5 FP on Spence's set). Any adapter carries its own client timeout <=2 s (hook timeout field is settable; 30 s default is unacceptable during latency incidents, which do not trip fail-open). On teams, enable per project not per developer. Skills only; files, context-map pointers, and tool calls have no measurement anywhere. Never 'core'. Confirm with TypeSafe in writing that BYOK harness use is 'developed and operated by Customer' under the 2026-09-23 MCA.
  10. Generation restricted to machine-checkable artifacts: deny patterns, hooks, scripts, CI checks — accepted by an exit-code check on inputs the generating agent did not author, identical on every harness, staged outside every harness-loaded directory (a SKILL.md in a skills dir is never inactive; it enters the listing and re-attaches after compaction) until merged through the normal PR path. No generated prose SKILL.md (SkillsBench v4: skill-creator output lands 8.1-11.5pp below no-skills). Before building any new namespace or ownership kind, instrument the harden loop Joycraft already ships (one stamped rule in two months, no fired-or-not surface) — gated generation is not new here, it is unmeasured.
  11. Architecture-defense as an opt-in mode of design/decide on existing code (Helix's direction: agent extracts architecture from code with file:line evidence, human confirms), not a universal setup step (gather-context.md:27 forbids the code scan for cost). Each correction terminates in the same commit as a harden deny pattern or CI dependency rule where path/regex-shaped, otherwise an owner-stamped decision-log row; no standalone architecture doc, no Context Map pointer. Extend verify Step 2.5 so the verifier's oracle reads those rows, and re-derive against code on evidence triggers (verify FINDING, folder-map drift, NEVER_READ telemetry), never on a calendar. One named owner per repo. Pilot with a pre-committed before/after count (verify FINDINGS per feature or the maintainer's hours of unshippable output).
  12. No per-user technical-background profile. Altitude is a project property set once by the repo owner in AGENTS.md beside the Execution Profile; gates, ceremony, checkpoint questions, specs, decision rows, PR bodies are one path per project. The only per-user residue is an uncommitted explanation-depth preference in docs/.joycraft/local/ (or Claude Code's per-user output style) inside the STE contract, built only after a named daily user who cannot read a diff exists. Instrument the brief's existing `User expertise` field (new-feature.md:181, zero consumers) first. P10 runs for everyone; the agent explains in STE rather than skipping the gate.
  13. Instruments before further ceremony: extend src/telemetry.ts to count Skill tool_use events (line 114 already recognizes them) so 'users forget the slash commands' becomes a number; stand up a claude plugin eval skill-trigger set with a no-plugin baseline; fix docs/context/dangerous-assumptions.md:14 (no-op window is six months, not 'since 2026-07'); fix the dogfood test 'keeps the intent inbox at its README only' which is red on this checkout at the inbox's first legitimate use. Re-run P0 only if, 30 days after items 1-4 ship, telemetry still shows the same non-invocation rate and the loop still ends unshippable at a measured rate.

The human's positions the panel moved

  • Q1 'Gates + lifecycle + artifacts fixed; process prose generated' — the generated half moved, unanimously across P0, P4, P8. Evidence: SkillsBench v4 (verified live by three judges) puts Anthropic-skill-creator-generated skills 8.1/11.3/11.5pp BELOW the no-skills baseline on Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI while curated add +18.2/+19.7/+24.8; Anthropic's skill-creator post classes encoded-team-process skills (which the 22 are) as the durable kind, 'only as valuable as their fidelity to your actual workflow'; ACE's one-rewrite collapse; omp ships autolearn default-off and 'experimental'; two of the three named failure causes ('packs the solver never discovers', 'confidently wrong pack content') are invisible to a visual reviewer, and the maintainer is the N=1 evaluator who per the repo's own level5 brief 'knows all the magic words'. Panel position: curated, shortened, eval-gated prose; generate only machine-checkable artifacts behind an exit-code gate. The invariant half did not move — every skeptic keeps gates, lifecycle, artifacts, the STE directive, 'the formality of the loop', and TDD — but P8's auditor showed 'the formality of the loop' is not separable from process prose in the current files (decompose's 3-7 specs / <=2 deps rules, verify's 70-line verifier prompt), so the maintainer must name which lines are formality before anything is cut.
  • Q2 'if I can get it to work best for me, we can easily get it for others' — moved on delivery, not on priority (P1, P2, P7, P9). Evidence: AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md are create-once (update-inventory.ts:236-262), so the router block — the only measured piece of P1 — never reaches the 15 colleagues without a new marker-patch kind the intent does not name; the checkpoint the maintainer calls 'amazing' is the Claude db-published page, and on Codex/Pi/omp/Copilot it is a paste-back block (RF-KILL-6) with the fixing server backlogged; Codex skill attribution is unavailable from shell strings (telemetry.ts:404) so a lead cannot audit divergence; the super-user's warm npx cache makes an @latest oracle look free while fifteen machines pay the drift; a harness tuned for someone who can recognize slop is exactly the one that fails a mixed-seniority engineer who cannot. 'Works for me → works for others' is a delivery claim today's updater cannot honor. Also: 'about 15 colleagues … of mixed skill' is asserted, not shown — no named daily user cannot read a diff.
  • Q3 'all I have to do is push the new prompting guide to an update and everyone gets the new juice' — moved on mechanism by all four P5 skeptics and confirmed by the judge; the park itself stands on hours but its reason does not. Evidence: the profile is already kind: vendor, ownership: verified (docs/.joycraft/manifest.json:951-955), replaced on every update with a backup, and main merges auto-release — PR #78 delivered the Fable profile exactly that way 22 days after the guide, so the wish is current behaviour and a fetch path adds a network module, cache, offline policy, fetch stubs, and a fourth ownership kind without changing the outcome. 'Everyone' is wrong for the maintainer's own fleet: model-profile.ts:20 keys the profile to the harness and AGENTS.md runs Pi on kimi-k3 and Codex on GPT-6, so a Qwen/Kimi run receives Anthropic steering. 'It may become moot' is unsupported: nothing in a fetch design removes the work the nine parked specs do, and parked spec 8 IS the subtract half of P5 already written. Hand condensation already dropped a sentence the vendor calls load-bearing ('The user is not watching in real time'). The panel did not reconcile whether to unpark (harness-expert) or audit-and-subtract only (auditor); this synthesis unparks specs 3 and 8.
  • Q4 'gates that cannot be overridden' / 'sit back and relax and have full confidence of when that loop is done they have shippable product' / 'we are already doing alot of what helix is doing' — diagnosis kept, cure and reading of Helix moved (P3, P9, P10). Evidence: no host sells a non-overridable hook — live Claude Code docs: a timed-out PreToolUse hook 'doesn't block the tool call … don't count on a stalled hook to act as a gate', Stop hooks block but Claude Code 'overrides the hook and ends the turn after 8 consecutive blocks'; Codex continues the tool call on hook error; only Pi tool_call fails closed and Joycraft writes no enforcement surface for Pi. In this repo .claude/settings.json is not on the deny list, the docs-sync gate passes on an agent-written 'Docs: none' line, block-dangerous.sh blocked nothing from 2026-03-24 to 2026-09-23 with a green test, and branch protection on main has zero required status checks. Helix's 'sit back' is not in the source: gate 4 is 'The engineer looks at the code and running app' at every checkpoint, checkpoints are 'the screen skeleton' then 'one deliberately small section', gates 1-2 diff against an existing reference app a greenfield spec lacks. 'Already doing a lot of what Helix does' holds for the tests gate and fails for the three judgment gates; Joycraft's version (verify-in-loop, designed 2026-05-28) has never been wired. The slop passed prose gates already non-overridable in wording (implement.md:105), so it is semantic; 'hours of unshippable slop' has no written record; and Q4 contradicts the maintainer's own D2 stamped one day earlier ('No continuation logic and no Stop-hook recipe … test whether the standing instruction is enough first').
  • Q5 'it should be a core part of the product now … route what files to look at, what pointers in the context map to look at, help claude code with tool calls' — flipped by all five P6 skeptics and the judge, back to the lead's advisory-first shape. Evidence: the only routing measurement does not transfer (Haiku 4.5 agent, 182 skills, 60-char Hermes-default descriptions, 488 synthetic Sonnet-5-authored requests the cookbook itself calls 'easier than the ones users send', jev-1.12, in-sample thresholds, 7 regressions, conclusion scoped to 'a large roster'); Joycraft is the inverse regime (22 skills, full descriptions at 42-49% of budget, frontier agents) and P1 shrinks the roster further; the only third-party Claude Code build got 3 wrong of 6 on a real session and says it is 'unlikely to help a strong model as a router'; 'insanely good' has no artifact (zero jev/typesafe references in src/, templates/, scripts/) and comes from in-app use, which TypeSafe's own coding-agents page endorses while saying Jev 'is not a drop-in replacement for the LLM behind Claude Code'; files, context-map pointers (one row exists), and tool calls have no measurement anywhere; two of the last three status-page incidents were latency, which does not trip fail-open; MCA is AS IS/AS AVAILABLE with no SLA; a model-free forced-eval hook measured 22/22 with 0/5 false positives. The maintainer's own list of wins (files, pointers, research, web scraping, panels) is mostly the off-hot-path advisory use. 'I'm open to the skeptics saying no of course' — on core, hot path, and for-anyone-with-a-key, this is that no; on Jev in Joycraft at all, it is not.
  • §0 'Users forget the many slash commands' and 'all 22 skills compete for auto-invocation' — moved (P1). The forgetting is nine human doors, not 22, and its cause is naming: descriptions are process jargon ('decompose', 'atomic specs', 'deny patterns') and only joycraft-setup's speaks in the user's words. At 3,339-3,955 chars the 22 sit well under the 8,000-char figure and below #64606's failure band; what competes with Joycraft is the hundreds of third-party plugin skills in the maintainer's own sessions, which a router block outside the listing and disable-model-invocation relieve and a 22→8 consolidation does not. The premise is unmeasured: docs/.joycraft/telemetry.json records doc reads only (14 sessions).
  • §0 architecture-defense 'the corrections become a core part of the context map' — moved (P10). The context-map panel's own verdict (2026-09-01, line 57) calls the Context Map 'hopeful disclosure, not progressive disclosure' and disqualifies must-read content from the pointer tier; verify Step 2.5 never reads it; harden cannot convert semantic rules. Corrections must terminate as checks or owner-stamped decision-log rows the verifier reads. The reported benefit ('much less slop') is one uncontrolled report from a non-user and could not be refuted, hence the pilot.
  • §0 'setup asks for the user's technical background, and that forks the abstraction level' — flipped (P11). It contradicts Q1 (a fork of gates/artifacts by user varies what Q1 fixes) and Q2 ('one path'; the maintainer's own prediction that the skill gap 'becomes a non issue' as the harness drives more); the brief's `User expertise: [comfortable / learning / needs guidance]` field has existed at new-feature.md:181 with zero consumers; BMAD removed user_skill_level tailoring in v6.11.0; Bing Copilot data (arXiv 2502.18685) says the expert register is fine regardless of user level while under-pitching hurts; pooled generic skills beat per-developer ones (arXiv 2608.10319); Shapiro's Levels 1-2 are developer collaboration modes, not a non-programmer tier, and Joycraft's own levels.md targets Levels 3-4.
  • P9 clarification 'stay in chat until the human or the agent signals the idea has crystallized' and 'I don't know yet … routes back to chat or to a panel' and 'panels as a standard step' — moved on three points (P9). The agent half of the clarity signal is dropped (no eval, no check, no precedent; decision-log 2026-05-30 kept risk judgment human because 'only a human knows'). 'Or to a panel' is rejected by the novice (41-53 KB adversarial documents) and the maintainer lens (no mechanism, no cost); 'back to chat' alone is rejected by the team-lead (chat has no owner); the panel converges on an owned open row that returns to chat. Panels are not standard: zero cost figures, Helix misread (no pre-code panel), the fully front-loaded Opus 5.5 feature approved (D9) and parked the same day. The maintainer's own behaviour supports the human-declared version: Q8 'no brief though, as you and I will have follow up discussion' and the pack's 'chat-only, no gate artifacts by request' origin are a person who knows when he is exploring — but that origin is also the Deposition Checkpoint pilot's unadjudicated kill signal ('kill the format if Max bypasses the questions into free chat by the second feature'), which must be re-read on the record.
  • Not moved, for the record: Q1's invariant half; Q4's goal sentence ('an attempt may be wrong but cannot ship until it is not'); Q2's priority (maintainer first); the want for code-computed state (every skeptic wants it, solo-pi more than the maintainer); 'no MCP main channel'; the belief that the architecture-defense practice reduces slop-on-slop (unrefuted, unmeasured).

Where the panel disagrees with the lead's synthesis

  • Section 9 frames P0 as 'reimagining vs incremental fixes'. That split is wrong: all four P0 skeptics and the judge found every verified pain maps to an existing mechanism (disable-model-invocation has 0 uses; five-tree fan-out is one table in sync-skills.mjs/generate-bundled-files.mjs; dropped skills already orphan cleanly in update-plan.ts:362-399; ownedRegion exists in the manifest), plus exactly one missing thing the incremental list omits: a blocking verify-in-loop gate. The count-sensitivity pillar does not apply at 3,339-3,955 chars against ~8,000 (#64606's own 22-skill project at 2,801 chars was unaffected). The generation pillar is contradicted by its own citation (SkillsBench v4: −8.1/−11.3/−11.5pp).
  • 'The invariant is the gate loop, not the prose' — half wrong on where the gate lives. The lead's item 3 puts it in 'deterministic checks and blocking hooks'. Hooks cannot deliver 'cannot be overridden': PreToolUse fails open on timeout, Stop caps at 8 blocks, hook registration is agent-editable here, block-dangerous.sh was a no-op for six months with a green test, pr-docs-gate.mjs needed a false-positive fix 2m40s after shipping. The invariant belongs at required CI on main (today zero required checks), the mark-done --to done precondition, the Pi loop driver's exit-code step, and a wired fresh-context verifier. Helix's confidence does not come from determinism: three of its four gates are Gemini review, two isolated reviewers, and per-checkpoint engineer approval.
  • 'Frontier models need less process, not less verification' cites arXiv 2609.20804 for something it did not measure. The paper ablated a planning tool + protocol on Nemotron-3 30B/120B/550B and Mistral-Medium-3.5 — no Claude/GPT/Gemini, no SKILL.md, no verification axis — and found that at the top tier structure SAVES cost (−30/−32%) with −2.0/−0.4pp accuracy. The verification half rests on qualitative vendor statements. The panel's replacement: cut ceremony and duplication (measured: SkillsBench compact +19.0/+21.5 vs comprehensive +0.7), keep protocol behind an eval; none of research/decompose/new-feature/verify 'dies'.
  • 'Discoverability has a measured fix … Count-sensitivity is measured (1% budget, #64606)'. The 1% budget and 'least-invoked drop first' are not on the Claude Code skills page; the constant comes from a binary analysis in an issue closed as not planned, and the drop order is the reporter's claim. The measured fix is the always-loaded router block only. The hub skill (candidate shape item 1) has no cited test anywhere (Superpowers has no hub, BMAD cut to 8 not 1, GSD's /gsd-next router is archived) and Joycraft already ships a hub-shaped door (joycraft-setup) with no inbound references and no invocation data. Forwarding shims are the exact pattern Superpowers deleted. Vercel's 100% measured one skill's docs retrieval, not routing among workflows, and its authors say skills suit 'vertical, action-specific workflows that users explicitly trigger' — a description of Joycraft's doors.
  • 'The human is currently the glue … Ten skills hand off through /clear. OpenSpec's CLI is the precedent for code-computed state.' Three errors. Mechanism: src/cli.ts has zero state-reading commands, the CLI is npx-resolved and this repo spent two of sixteen 0.7.x releases on stale-npx behaviour; the maintainer's own check.mjs vendored-script pattern is the correct shape, and OpenSpec's troubleshooting admits the stale-CLI drift the lead's precedent imports. Motive: the /clear handoffs are justified in the skills as context hygiene, not missing state; a fresh context is a harness primitive (context: fork, pi -p), not a state query. Urgency: 0 queue/frontmatter mismatches across 131 specs; the only recorded silent state lie came from the existing code oracle (joycraft-mark-done exit-0 no-op, 2026-07-27), not from prose.
  • 'Model profiles: fetch, subtract, eval … Claude Code already injects the Fable block.' Fetch is refuted: the profile is already kind: vendor replaced on every update with automatic release, so 'push the guide to an update' is today's behaviour; the 6,610-word vendor page is mostly API-only and the labor is selection/condensation, which fetch does not remove; seven skills cite the profile by heading and a test enforces it; slugs cannot be constructed (sibling guesses 404), pages carry no ETag/Last-Modified. The Codex openai-docs 'precedent' is a docs-lookup skill; Codex's real per-model steering is bundled models.json. 'Claude Code already injects the Fable block' is only partly true: the batching instruction is verbatim in the system prompt, the autonomy block is not confirmed and is absent for subagents. Subtract stands (optimize Step 2c already ships it).
  • 'Distribution: two skill dirs + Claude plugin + CLI'. The plugin leg survives only as a git-committed project-scope skills-dir plugin; a marketplace plugin is refuted: auto-update is off by default for third-party marketplaces with no field to turn it on, running sessions keep old versions, a committed enabledPlugins entry does not fetch the plugin onto a teammate's machine, install hints require an Anthropic-named marketplace (the lead's own §2.7 says so and §2's inference ignores it), and skills reference docs/templates/ 77 times and docs/.joycraft/ 13 times — CLI-installed files the manifest has no kind to version-lock against a plugin. 'One skills tree' is not a table change: today's trees differ by 141 skill_prefix sites and real body forks.
  • Candidate shape item 4, 'Generation as a gated proposal loop … inactive until an eval or a human accepts', should be dropped for prose skills. Neither gate exists in Joycraft's setting: check.sh has no baseline arm and cannot see which skill ran ('Joycraft ships it and never runs it'); claude plugin eval is Claude-only, N=3, and has Claude propose its own cases; a human-accepted agent draft is by definition a curated skill, so the delta over curated is undefined. The one gated loop already shipped (harden) has one stamped rule in two months and no outcome record. Only machine-checkable artifacts behind an exit-code gate survive.
  • Candidate shape item 8 and the P9 clarification, 'panels, dialoguing artifacts, and pre-spec diagrams/prototypes as standard (risk-tiered) gates … consistent with Helix'. Helix, verified live, has no pre-code design, diagram, prototype, or panel step; the engineer approves a checkpoint sequence 'in minutes' and reviews 'the code and running app'. It supports P3/Q4 (gates on implemented checkpoints), not design-bookend ceremony. Panels have zero skill mechanism and zero cost figures; the existing design gate is skipped in 13 of 23 spec'd features; the fully front-loaded Opus 5.5 feature was parked the day it was approved. Only the clarity-timed checkpoint and the __explore escape survive, and the agent-detected-clarity half is dropped.
  • The lead's item 3 recommendation on Jev (advisory, off the hot path first) was right, and the panel restores it against the maintainer's override — but tightens it: not 'core' ever without a held-out eval on Joycraft's roster, shadow-mode router before any inject mode, skills only, <=2 s client timeout, per-project enablement on teams.
  • P10 and P11 as drafted in §9 both borrow authority they do not have: P10's 'enforceable architecture record' has no mechanism (harden.md:33-40 classes semantic rules ineligible; verify Step 2.5 never reads the decision log; implement reads nothing under docs/context) and inverts Helix (human-designed architecture, reviewers enforce over code); P11 contradicts the maintainer's own Q1/Q2 frame and its only shipped precedent (BMAD user_skill_level) was removed 2026-08-09.
  • Omissions in §9 that the panel found decisive: delivery to existing installs (AGENTS.md is create-once; the only post-creation edit is the model-profile row patch); branch protection on main has zero required status checks; no failure analysis of the Q4 slop exists anywhere in the repo; the maintainer's D2 (2026-09-23) forbids exactly the completion gate Q4 asks for; verify on Pi depends on a `subagent` tool stock Pi lacks and the pipeline extension does not register; the newest shipped mechanism (intent inbox) is red in tests/dogfood-update.test.ts on this checkout.

Open risks

  • The entire gate program is built for a failure with no written record. If the failure analysis shows the slop was spec quality or model choice rather than absent verification, even the sixth incremental item is unwarranted; if it shows semantic failure (green tests, wrong behaviour), deterministic checks cannot see it and the verifier plus a human checkpoint is the whole answer — the panel did not agree whether a greenfield spec can ever be 'shippable at loop end' without a human checkpoint.
  • Silent no-op recurrence. block-dangerous.sh blocked nothing for six months with a green test encoding the wrong contract; pr-docs-gate.mjs misfired 2m40s after shipping; no Joycraft gate has an observed fire rate or false-positive rate. Any new gate without a host-faithful contract test and a fired-or-not surface is Ronacher's 'appears more robust' by construction, and it retires vigilance.
  • The agent authors what any gate reads. ImpossibleBench: frontier models cheat ~50% on visible spec-test conflicts, monitors catch 42-50%, the DGM deleted its detector's markers. Unless verify reads locked/held-out tests or CI on the branch, the 'gate' is an agent-satisfiable check that looks enforced.
  • Delivery to existing installs. Router block, folder-map repair, clarity sentence, and any AGENTS.md change all depend on a marker-patch ownership kind that does not exist; the manifest's three kinds (vendor | create-once | config-patch) have no home for it, and each new mechanism has cost a red suite (intent inbox is red on this checkout at first real use; suite is 230 s).
  • The 'one skills tree' is a prose rewrite, not a table change: 141 {{skill_prefix}}, 21 {{clear}}, 13 {{skills_dir}} substitution sites plus body forks in four skills. Pi's runtime read path is untraced (Joycraft installs .pi/skills, which current Pi docs do not list; solo-pi says resource-loader.ts hard-codes .pi/skills), and Copilot dedupe across .claude/skills and .agents/skills has two contradictory readings of the same page. A wrong call here silently serves Codex invocation syntax to Pi users.
  • The open-weight tier. AGENTS.md dispatches Pi on kimi-k3; the Pi tree is already the shortest; the only skills-directory study says mid-tier models gain 6-7x more from skill content than frontier; Joycraft has zero evals on any model; no open-weight vendor publishes subtractive steering to fetch. Every prose cut and every profile change lands on this tier untested, and 'everyone gets the new juice' excludes it by construction.
  • Verify on Pi depends on a `subagent` tool with agent joycraft-verifier that stock Pi does not ship and Joycraft's pipeline extension does not register (grep = 0). The pillar the whole program keeps is the least guaranteed one on the harness the solo lens represents. Codex, Copilot, and omp have no context: fork equivalent and no enforcement surface, so the human stays glue and hooks stay advisory there regardless of design.
  • The vendored oracle's 2026-07-27 bugfix row is still in-review with no end-to-end autonomous-loop verification; a false 'Pipeline complete' ends a loop before spec 1. Two status stores (22 May specs have no frontmatter status) remain until the oracle becomes sole writer.
  • Q4 vs D2. The maintainer stamped 'No continuation logic and no Stop-hook recipe … test whether the standing instruction is enough first' on 2026-09-23 and asked for non-overridable gates on 2026-09-24. Both live on branches; neither ruling references the other.
  • The Q3 direction is unreconciled: harness-expert says unpark and finish spec 3; the auditor says the verified vendor message is audit-and-subtract, push nothing. This synthesis unparks specs 3 and 8 only; the other seven parked specs' fate is undecided, and the profile is drifting from vendor mirror into house style (End State of Every Prompt), which is either curated value or unmeasured accretion — no with/without run exists to say which.
  • Router-block wording. Superpowers issue #2377 (2026-09-24, open) reports pressure-language bootstraps making Fable 5.1 escalate trivial requests into multi-hour spec+planning runs. An always-loaded router written with 'MUST invoke' phrasing reproduces that on the maintainer's daily driver.
  • Jev shadow mode needs skill attribution that telemetry cannot provide on Codex, and the licensing hedge (BYOK under 'developed and operated by Customer') is unconfirmed in writing; a 60-day status window with latency incidents would leave the hot-path door closed indefinitely.
  • Cost of the checkpoint program on non-Claude harnesses: every gate ceremony added before the local checkpoint server ships lands as paste-back (RF-KILL-6) on four of five harnesses, and the Deposition Checkpoint's kill criterion has already been tripped by the maintainer without adjudication.
  • Two panels (Q6: Codex/Astra runs separately) may disagree; this synthesis has seen only the Claude side. The maintainer said he would compare both before any brief, spec, or stamp.
P0 · 4 skeptics

A reimagining is warranted at all

qualify
Ruling

P0 stands only in a narrow reading: "reimagining" means a subtraction-and-consolidation program on the existing architecture (two skill dirs, disable-model-invocation on the 11 agent-entry skills, a compact router block in AGENTS.md, folder-map promoted to a regenerable owned region, hub + forwarding shims through the existing orphan machinery, prose cut for frontier models) plus ONE item the skeptic's incremental list omits: a deterministic, blocking verify-in-loop gate on the implement loop, committed and identical for every user. The "dynamic" half as written — agent-generated process prose, Jev routing on the hot path, runtime-fetched model guidance, a plugin as a second distribution format — is not warranted on the current evidence and is contradicted by the one primary study that measures it.

The claim as argued

Joycraft should be reimagined as a dynamic, gate-driven harness rather than fixed incrementally. The skeptic case: the incremental fixes (publish skills to .agents/skills + .claude/skills, mark internal skills disable-model-invocation, repair the write-once folder map, add forwarding shims, rewrite descriptions in users' words) capture most of the value at a fraction of the cost and risk.

Replacement claim

Joycraft should be consolidated and hardened, not reimagined: a subtraction program on the current architecture (two skill dirs, disable-model-invocation on internals, AGENTS.md router block, regenerable folder map, hub + shims, prose cut) plus one new blocking verify-in-loop gate captures every verified pain; the 'dynamic' components (generated process prose, Jev hot-path routing, runtime-fetched guidance, plugin distribution) are deferred pending a measured residual after that set ships.

Condition

P0 holds if and only if "reimagining" is read as: (1) the six subtraction/consolidation items delivered as an ordinary versioned update through existing machinery — publish one skills tree to .agents/skills + .claude/skills; `disable-model-invocation: true` on the 11 `entry: agent` skills; a compact routing block in AGENTS.md written in users' words; the folder-map sentinel promoted from create-once to a regenerable owned region (fixing tune.md:63's broken promise); hub skill + forwarding shims via the existing drop/orphan path in src/update-plan.ts; step-by-step prose cut in the 12 skills over 200 lines — PLUS (2) one deterministic, blocking verify-in-loop gate on the implement loop, committed and byte-identical on every machine, registered and covered by a hook stdin-fixture test, and preceded by at least one recorded green-but-unshippable case in docs/discoveries with its root cause. It falls if "reimagining" includes any of: agent-generated process prose or skills/hooks with a fourth ownership kind, Jev on the hot path or as a core dependency, a Claude plugin as a second distribution format, or a runtime fetch path for model guidance — until, 30 days after (1)+(2) ship, `joycraft telemetry` or a skill-trigger eval shows a measured residual (non-invocation or unshippable loop endings) that the shipped set did not close.

Judge's reasoning

Four skeptics returned: three "qualified" (maintainer, team-lead, evidence-auditor) and one "refuted" (harness-expert). All four converge on the same shape, so the ruling is a qualification, not a keep or a flip. I verified the load-bearing repo facts myself rather than take either side's count. (1) The incremental fixes really are cheap in this repo: `disable-model-invocation` has zero uses across src/ and scripts/; 11 skills already carry `entry: agent`; the five-tree fan-out is one table in scripts/sync-skills.mjs and scripts/generate-bundled-files.mjs; dropped skills are already deleted-or-orphaned by src/update-plan.ts; the folder-map bug is exactly what all four say — `materializeDocuments` in src/update-inventory.ts:227-262 returns [] for any existing create-once document, so `ensureFolderMapSection` is unreachable after first creation while src/skills/joycraft-tune.md:63 still promises "upgrade regenerates it", and this repo's AGENTS.md has zero mentions of docs/intent. (2) The "22 skills overflow the budget" pillar does not apply at Joycraft's size: shipped Claude tree descriptions total 3,339 chars (canonical file, 24 lines incl. 3 harness variants, 3,619) against the ~8,000-char budget documented in issue #64606, whose own table lists a 22-skill project at 2,801 chars / 35% unaffected. (3) The "generate process prose" pillar is contradicted by its own citation: all four skeptics independently fetched arXiv 2602.12670 v4 and found self-generated skills BELOW the no-skills baseline (−8.1 pp Claude Code+Opus 4.7, −11.3 pp Codex+GPT-5.5, −11.5 pp Gemini CLI) while curated skills add +16.6 pp; the pack cited older numbers ("no benefit on average"). Anthropic's skill-creator post (hedged: "may become less necessary… evals tell you when") classifies encoded-team-process skills — which is what Joycraft's 22 skills are — as the durable kind. (4) The single justification that survives for anything beyond the incremental list is the maintainer's Q4 report of hours of unshippable output. That is real as a gap (verify-in-loop is explicitly unshipped per src/skills/joycraft-session-end.md:138) but has zero written record: grep for slop/unshippable across docs/discoveries, docs/context, docs/backlog hits only STE prose rules. A gate is still the right instrument — but it is a bounded feature on the current harness, not evidence the harness needs rebuilding. The precedent the pack leans on cuts the same way: Joycraft's one auto-registered gate (block-dangerous.sh) silently never blocked for ~6 months (CHANGELOG.md:28), which argues for register-and-test, not generate. (5) Q3's wish is already the current system: the profile doc is a vendor-kind file replaced on `npx joycraft update` (src/model-profile.ts, src/install-manifest.ts:30) and release is automatic on merge (AGENTS.md "Release behavior"); a fetch path adds a network path, cache, fallback, and test family without changing the outcome. (6) The maintainer's marginal-cost exhibit holds: I ran tests/dogfood-update.test.ts and "keeps the intent inbox at its README only" fails because docs/intent/2026-09-24-dynamic-joycraft.md exists — though I read this as a too-strict dogfood assertion meeting its first real intent, not proof the inbox mechanism is wrong. Net: every verified pain maps to an existing code path or a one-line frontmatter change, plus one missing gate. Nothing verified requires a new architecture, and the "dynamic" components have null-to-negative primary evidence.

Strongest refutation considered

The harness-expert's outright "refuted": every named pain (discoverability, five copies, folder map, human-as-glue, push-the-guide, slop) already maps onto an existing mechanism — `disable-model-invocation`, a two-array target list, `ownedRegion` in the manifest, Claude Code's `context: fork` frontmatter, the vendor-kind profile file, and four shipped-but-unregistered gate hook recipes — so a rewrite adds a second surface to a solo-maintained 10.7k-LOC updater while the incremental list removes surface. I did not adopt the full refutation for two reasons. First, three of the four skeptics (and the human's Q4) identify a gap the skeptic's five-item list does not cover: a blocking verify-in-loop gate is not on it, and `context: fork` is Claude-only so it does not close the 13-file `{{clear}}` handoff problem on Codex, Pi, Copilot or omp. Second, "refuted" overstates what the evidence shows — the evidence shows the reimagining is unproven and its generation pillar is measured negative, which is a qualification with a condition, not a demonstrated falsehood.

Human position moved?

Q1 (gates + lifecycle + artifacts fixed; process prose GENERATED): first half kept by all four; second half moved by all four. Evidence: SkillsBench v4 puts self-generated skills 8–11.5 pp below no skills; Anthropic's skill-creator post classifies encoded team-process skills as the durable kind; ACE's one-rewrite collapse (18,282→122 tokens, below baseline); omp ships autolearn default-off and experimental. Panel position: cut the prose (12 of 22 skills exceed 200 lines) and keep what remains committed and reviewed — generate less, do not generate. The STE directive, loop formality, and TDD habit the human names as the core are all installed today and untouched by the incremental path, which argues for keeping the architecture. Q2 (maintainer first, colleagues second, one path): partially moved by the team-lead — 'easily get it for others' is asserted, not evidenced; a harness tuned for a super-user who can recognize slop is exactly the one that fails a mixed-seniority engineer who cannot; no study compares entry-point counts or onboarding. Maintainer and harness-expert read Q2 as supporting incremental (a solo super-user with automatic release needs fewer files to keep green, not distribution machinery). Q3 (park Opus 5.5; 'push the guide and everyone gets the new juice'): moved by all four, in two directions the panel did not reconcile. All agree the literal wish is today's mechanism (vendor-kind profile file + automatic release), so a fetch path adds cost without changing the outcome. Harness-expert says unpark and finish spec 3; evidence-auditor says the verified vendor message (Fable 5 guide: 'review and consider removing older instructions'; skill-creator: 'evals tell you when') is audit-and-subtract, not push. Q4 (Helix gates that cannot be overridden; recent slop): diagnosis kept by all four — this is the one gap the skeptic's incremental list does not close, and verify-in-loop is verifiably unshipped. Cure moved: a bounded, committed, deterministic blocking verify gate on the current harness, registered and tested (the existing safeguard hook never blocked for six months), not a re-architecture. Maintainer and auditor add: write down at least one case / produce telemetry first, because no record of the slop exists anywhere in the repo. Q5 (Jev routing on the hot path, core, for anyone with a key): flipped by all four. Per-user-key-only licensing, no SLA, 99.826% uptime, fail-open PreToolUse hooks, and an SDK that broke compatibility four days after shipping mean five engineers would get five routings; a fail-open hook cannot be a gate. Panel position: opt-in advisory off the hot path, not core. P0 does not depend on Jev either way.

Skeptic disagreements

  • Verdict split: harness-expert says 'refuted'; maintainer, team-lead and evidence-auditor say 'qualified'. Same evidence, different threshold for what counts as a reimagining.
  • What the incremental list is missing: maintainer says add a verify gate only AFTER one green-but-unshippable case is recorded in docs/discoveries with root cause; team-lead and harness-expert say wire it now as a sixth incremental item; evidence-auditor says produce `joycraft telemetry` numbers first and instead adds a CLI state-query command as the missing item (OpenSpec 1.0.0 precedent).
  • Whether hub + forwarding shims is 'reimagining' or 'incremental': maintainer places it inside the permitted subtraction program; harness-expert treats it as already-incremental; team-lead cites BMAD 14→8 with shims as an ordinary release.
  • Description budget size: harness-expert 3,347 chars, evidence-auditor 3,619 chars. Both are right on different bases — I measured 3,339 in the shipped Claude tree (22 lines) and 3,619 in canonical src/skills (24 lines incl. 3 implement-feature harness variants). Neither approaches the ~8,000 budget.
  • Skills over optimize's 200-line limit: pack, maintainer and harness-expert say 10; evidence-auditor says 12. I measured 12.
  • Human-glue handoff count: pack/team-lead/auditor say 10 skills; maintainer and harness-expert say 13 files / 21 `{{clear}}` occurrences. I measured 13 files, 21 occurrences, 9 files with 'briefing'; 10 matches the briefing/new-session pattern. Different definitions, same direction.
  • Q3 (push the guide): maintainer says keep the vendor channel and write fewer blocks; harness-expert says unpark feature/opus-5-5-prompting and finish spec 3 (swap-profile-row-on-update); evidence-auditor says the vendor message is 'audit and subtract', so run optimize-flags-stale-rules instead of pushing anything.
  • Q5 (Jev): all four reject core-on-hot-path, but degree differs — maintainer flips outright yet will carry opt-in off the hot path; harness-expert says opt-in hook on today's harness; team-lead says cannot be core while per-user-key/fail-open/99.8%; auditor says enthusiasm is not evidence and P0 does not depend on it.
  • Source of the '1% of context' listing budget: maintainer and auditor say not found on any official page; harness-expert attributes it to issue #64606 (`skillListingBudgetFraction = 0.01`). I verified the issue body contains that constant from a binary analysis of v2.1.159 — the fact is corroborated by a third-party reverse-engineering, not by an official doc, so the pack's placement under §2.2 as if official is a misattribution.
  • Superpowers slash-command removal date: harness-expert marks the citation 'holds'; evidence-auditor marks 'misread' (v5.1.0 published 2026-05-04, not 2026-04-30). I verified via GitHub API: 2026-05-04T22:13Z. Auditor is right; the error is minor and does not change the direction.
  • Whether the red dogfood test is evidence: only the maintainer cites tests/dogfood-update.test.ts failing as proof that each new mechanism costs a red suite. I confirmed the failure but read it as a too-strict assertion ('README only') meeting the inbox's first legitimate use, not as a defect in the mechanism.

  • Pack §9 P7 '2026-03 deferral reason was avoiding two formats': UNVERIFIED — decision log has only the 2026-03-24 joycraft-* namespacing row (docs/context/decision-log.md:101), no plugin-deferral row (maintainer).
  • Human Q4 'hours of unshippable slop': UNVERIFIED as a fact — no discovery, decision-log row, backlog item, session ID, count, or telemetry output; the pack §10 treats it as a fact the frame adds.

What would change the ruling

Toward keep (full reimagining warranted): (a) at least three recorded green-but-unshippable implement-loop cases in docs/discoveries, each with root cause, showing the failure is in skill routing or prose-driven process that a deterministic check plus verify-in-loop cannot catch; (b) 30 days after the incremental set ships, `joycraft telemetry` or a `claude plugin eval` skill-trigger set still showing the same non-invocation rate and the loop still ending unshippable at a measured rate; (c) a primary study showing gated self-generated process skills beating curated skills in the software-engineering domain for the target models (the current best, SkillOpt, is eval-gated refinement of existing skills, not generation from nothing); (d) evidence that a Codex/Pi/Copilot/omp user cannot get a blocking verify gate through committed files, forcing a runtime component. Toward flip (incremental only, no gate needed): a record showing the recent unshippable sessions were caused by spec quality or model choice rather than absence of verification — then even the sixth item is not warranted and the skeptic's five-item list stands as the whole program.

Skeptics

Maintainer counting hoursqualified
Strongest refutation

The costs the thesis blames on the current shape are mostly not maintainer hours, and the value the reimagining promises is mostly reachable by deletion and one missing gate. (1) "Five per-harness copies" are one canonical source run through a 233-line applyTemplate (scripts/lib/skill-template.mjs) and `pnpm sync-skills` (scripts/sync-skills.mjs:38-44, 68-90); a byte-equality test guards them. The real fork cost is 75 `<!-- harness:X -->` markers across 22 files, and collapsing five output dirs to two removes zero of those markers. (2) "Gated on the maintainer's release cadence" is false in this repo: release is automatic on merge (AGENTS.md "Release behavior"; CHANGELOG.md header), 25 tags between 2026-06-15 and 2026-09-23. The human's Q3 wish, "push the new prompting guide to an update and everyone gets the new juice", is what a vendor-kind template already does today: the profile doc is a vendor file at src/model-profile.ts:14-24 delivered by `npx joycraft update`; no fetch path is needed to get that outcome. (3) The incremental fixes are each a frontmatter line or an existing code path: `disable-model-invocation` has 0 uses (grep src/skills) and the generator can emit it under a claude block; dropped or renamed skills are already removed cleanly with orphan protection (src/update-plan.ts:362-399), so hub+shims needs no new update machinery; the `.agents/skills` target already exists (sync-skills.mjs:40). (4) The one justification for a re-architecture around blocking gates, "hours of unshippable slop", has no record anywhere in docs/discoveries or docs/context (grep for slop/unshippable finds only STE prose rules), while the loop already demands green tests before advancing (src/skills/joycraft-implement.md:86-105; joycraft-implement-feature.md:61,116). Green-but-unshippable is a verify/spec-quality failure with an unknown root cause, and you cannot design a gate for a failure you have not recorded once. (5) Every genuinely new mechanism in the candidate shape carries a named bill here: a fourth ownership kind touches src/install-manifest.ts:30, the 420-line action classifier in src/update-plan.ts, src/update-inventory.ts, the legacy prefix bridge (install-manifest.ts:293-297), and 14 test files (67 kind mentions); blocking hooks need four new adapters because the shipped Pi extension registers no hook events (src/templates/pi-extensions/joycraft-pipeline.ts, 63 lines) and Codex/Copilot/omp have none; a Jev adapter adds keys, fail-open paths and outage support for 15 colleagues against an SDK that broke compatibility four days after shipping (pack §7.3); a plugin adds a second distribution format; a fetch path repeats the ~430-line update-check.ts pattern. (6) The marginal-cost curve is visible right now: the intent inbox shipped 2026-09-23 (PR #78) and the first real intent filed, this feature's own, breaks `tests/dogfood-update.test.ts › keeps the intent inbox at its README only`. One mechanism, one week, one red suite. (7) The live SkillsBench paper is harsher than the pack: self-generated skills land below the no-skills baseline (−8.1 to −11.5 pp) while curated skills add +18.2 to +24.8 pp, so "generate skills on the fly" is negative-value work for the maintainer to build and guard.

Qualification

P0 stands only if \"reimagining\" means a subtraction-and-consolidation program: hub skill plus forwarding shims (no new update machinery), `disable-model-invocation` on internals, a compact router block in AGENTS.md, folder-map sentinel promoted to a config-patch region, step-by-step prose cut for frontier models, and a deterministic verify-in-loop gate added only after at least one green-but-unshippable case is recorded in docs/discoveries with its root cause. It falls if \"reimagining\" includes any of: agent-generated skills/hooks with a fourth ownership kind, Jev on the hot path or as a core dependency, a Claude plugin as a second distribution format, or a runtime fetch path for model guidance — none of which has demand evidence at 453 downloads/month and ~15 users, and each of which adds a test family to a 230-second suite that is already red on this checkout because of last week's mechanism.

On the human's position

Q3: \"all I have to do is push the new prompting guide to an update and everyone gets the new juice.\" That is today's system. The profile doc is a vendor-kind template (src/model-profile.ts:14-24) and `npx joycraft update` replaces it; the SessionStart checker already nudges once per conversation. What costs hours is not delivery but authoring the condensed blocks, and a fetch path does not remove that work; it adds a network path, a cache, a bundled fallback that still needs updating, and a test family. My lens does not move Q3 toward fetch; it moves it toward \"keep the vendor channel, write fewer blocks.\" Q4: \"in recent sessions I've been getting some slop that took hours and that was not shippable, we have to close that gap.\" I agree the gap is the one thing the incremental list does not cover, but nothing in docs/discoveries records a single case, and the loop already requires green tests (joycraft-implement.md:86-105). Until one failure is written down (what was green, what was unshippable, which skill let it through), a gate is a mechanism designed against a rumor; the cheapest closing move is the verify-in-loop spec session-end.md:138 already names, not a re-architecture. Q5: \"it should be core part of the product now.\" From the hours ledger this is the single most expensive item on the table: an adapter per harness (four of five have no hook surface in Joycraft today), per-user keys, fail-open paths that must be tested, and outage triage for fifteen colleagues against an SDK that broke compatibility four days after release. Core-on-the-hot-path is the one position my lens flips outright; opt-in off the hot path I can carry. Q1: \"gates + lifecycle + artifacts fixed; process prose generated.\" Generated prose needs a generator, a namespace, an ownership kind, and a collapse guard (ACE went 18,282→122 tokens); deleted prose needs a diff. Both leave frontier models with the gates, and one of them has negative maintenance. Q2 \"me truly first\": consistent with my lens — a solo super-user with automatic release does not need distribution machinery; he needs fewer files to keep green.

Agent-harness expertrefuted
Strongest refutation

Every pain the intent names already maps onto a change the existing machinery supports, and the only parts of the "reimagining" that are not on the incremental list (agent-generated process prose, self-built skills/hooks, Jev on the hot path) are the parts with null-to-negative evidence. Concretely: (1) discoverability — Joycraft's 22 descriptions total 3,347 chars (src/skills/*.md frontmatter), about 42% of the ~8,000-char listing budget documented in claude-code#64606; the 11 `entry: agent` skills already carry the metadata to receive `disable-model-invocation: true`, and applyTemplate (scripts/lib/skill-template.mjs:56-99) already rewrites frontmatter per harness, so this is a one-line-per-skill change plus a routing block in AGENTS.md — the exact shape Vercel measured at 100% (vercel.com/blog/agents-md-outperforms-skills-in-our-agent-evals, 2026-01-27). (2) Five copies → two dirs: sync-skills.mjs TARGETS (scripts/sync-skills.mjs:38-44) and HARNESS_TARGETS (scripts/generate-bundled-files.mjs:53-59) are two arrays; cross-harness pack §3.3 shows `.agents/skills` + `.claude/skills` reach every surveyed harness. (3) Folder map never regenerated: root cause is update-inventory.ts:236-262 returning [] for an existing create-once doc; install-manifest.ts:44 already has `ownedRegion` for config-patch ownership — a sentinel-region patch kind is the fix, not a new architecture. (4) Human-as-glue: 13 skills carry `{{clear}}` handoffs; Claude Code's `context: fork` + `agent` frontmatter (code.claude.com/docs/en/skills.md, fetched 2026-09-24) runs a downstream skill in a fresh subagent with no /clear — a frontmatter edit, not a CLI oracle. (5) "Push the new prompting guide and everyone gets the new juice": the model profile is already a vendor-kind file replaced on every `update` (install-manifest.ts:30; update-plan.ts orphan/preserve rules), and the parked branch has D1–D9 stamped with 9 specs that do exactly this — parking it discards the incremental path already 80% designed. (6) Slop from the implement loop: Helix's answer is blocking gates, and Joycraft ships four gate hook recipes (src/templates/hooks/exit-code-gate.sh, test-file-lock.sh, protected-path-guard.sh, plan-sync-on-completion.sh, added 2026-09-22 be03794) that are "never registered" by design (src/templates/hooks/README.md:7-8), while the one auto-registered gate (block-dangerous.sh, added 2026-03-24 73bfd3f) silently never blocked for six months (CHANGELOG "Fixed: the safeguard hook never blocked"). That is the production failure mode of gate-driven harnesses — hooks fail silently and fail open — and it is fixed by registering and testing hooks (`claude plugin eval`, hook stdin fixtures), not by generating them. Meanwhile the live SkillsBench paper (arxiv.org/html/2602.12670) now reports self-generated skills BELOW the no-skills baseline (−8.1 to −11.5 pp across Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI), omp ships its own self-authoring behind `autolearn.enabled=false` labelled experimental (pack §1.6), and Ronacher's accretion warning (lucumr 2026-06-23) describes precisely a solo-maintained 10.7k-LOC updater (src/*.ts excl. bundle) + 5,573-line skill set that has shipped 15 releases and 32 merged PRs since June. A rewrite adds a second surface to keep alive; the incremental list removes surface.

Qualification

Re-open P0 only if, 30 days after shipping the incremental list (two skill dirs, disable-model-invocation on the 11 agent-entry skills, AGENTS.md routing block, folder-map ownedRegion patch, context: fork handoffs, registered + tested gate hooks with verify-in-loop), a `claude plugin eval` skill-trigger set and `joycraft telemetry` still show the same non-invocation and the implement loop still ends on unshippable output. Until that measurement exists, the reimagining has no baseline to beat.

On the human's position

Q1 — "Gates + lifecycle + artifacts fixed; process prose generated." The first half I keep; the second half my lens flips. The live SkillsBench numbers put self-generated skills 8–11.5 pp below no skills at all, omp ships the same idea default-off and experimental, and ACE's one-rewrite collapse (18,282→122 tokens, below baseline) is what "generated process prose" looks like in production. Generate less, do not generate: cut the prose (10 of 22 skills exceed optimize's own 200-line limit) and keep what remains committed and reviewed. Q3 — "all I have to do is push the new prompting guide to an update and everyone gets the new juice." That capability exists today: the profile is a vendor-kind file the updater replaces on every release (install-manifest.ts:30), and the parked branch's spec 3 (swap-profile-row-on-update) finishes the wiring. Parking it to wait for a reimagining postpones the thing you asked for. Q4 — "once they get to the implementation loop it's basically sit back and relax… we have to close that gap." Agreed on the gap, disagreed on the cure. Joycraft's one registered gate never blocked for six months and nobody noticed (CHANGELOG, 73bfd3f→fix); four more gate recipes ship unregistered by design. The gap is register-and-test, plus a code-driven implement loop with verify-in-loop — a bounded feature on the current harness, not evidence that the harness needs reimagining. Q5 — Jev on the hot path: outside P0's core, but from the hook seat it argues against the rewrite, not for it — PreToolUse hooks fail open on timeout, so a hot-path judge cannot be a gate; it is an opt-in hook you can add to today's harness. Q2 — "me truly first… 15 colleagues daily": fifteen daily users on five harness trees is the strongest reason to ship the six incremental fixes this month and measure with `/skill-doctor` and `joycraft telemetry` before touching the architecture. My lens does not move Q1's first half or Q4's diagnosis; it moves Q1's second half and Q3 from 'reimagine' to 'finish and prune'.

Team lead, five engineersqualified
Strongest refutation

For a team, the "dynamic" half of the proposition is not just unproven but measured to be negative, and the "gate" half does not need a reimagining. SkillsBench v4 (arXiv 2602.12670v4, 2026-06-14, live) now says self-generated skills land BELOW the no-skill baseline on every configuration tested — −8.1 pp on Claude Code + Opus 4.7, −11.3 pp on Codex + GPT-5.5 — and attributes it to "generated packs the solver never discovers, creator-side authoring that displaces solver work, and confidently wrong pack content." Those three failure modes are exactly what a reviewer of five engineers' PRs would have to catch on top of the code. Anthropic's own skill-creator post (claude.com/blog/improving-skill-creator-test-measure-and-refine-agent-skills) says capability-uplift skills "may become less necessary as models improve" but encoded-preference skills — "the skill sequences them according to your team's process" — are "more durable." Joycraft's 22 skills are encoded team process; the thesis that frontier models outgrew them applies to the other category. Meanwhile the discoverability fix with the only measured 100% result is a static always-loaded AGENTS.md index (Vercel, 2026-01-27: no docs 53%, skill 53%, explicit instruction 79%, 8KB index 100%), and the consolidation-with-shims precedent (BMAD core 14→8, v6-shims/ forwarding every retired ID) shipped as an ordinary release. In this repo the incremental list is cheap because the machinery already exists: zero skills set disable-model-invocation (grep of src/skills/*.md), the five-tree fan-out is a six-line table (scripts/generate-bundled-files.mjs:52-58, 178-184), removed skills are already deleted-if-verified/orphaned-if-edited (src/update-plan.ts:385-400), and the folder map's regen call exists (src/improve-claude-md.ts:412-415, src/agents-md.ts:148) but is unreachable after creation because src/update-inventory.ts:236-263 skips any existing create-once document — a narrow patch in the same shape as the existing contextMapPointerPatch. What the incremental list misses is the one thing the maintainer actually bleeds from (Q4: "slop that took hours and was not shippable"): a blocking verification step in the implement loop — session-end still says verify-in-loop has not shipped (§8.1). That is a sixth incremental item (committed hook + wired verify, identical for all five developers), not a new architecture. Jev routing on the hot path, per-user keys only, 99.826% uptime, fail-open, means five engineers get five different routings depending on who has a key and whether the service is up — the opposite of what a team lead is trying to buy.

Qualification

P0 survives only if "reimagining" is narrowed to its gate half: blocking, deterministic verification wired into the implement loop as committed, reviewed files identical on every developer's machine (a test/exit-code gate plus the unshipped verify-in-loop), delivered as an ordinary versioned update. Under that reading the incremental list needs a sixth item, not a new architecture. As written — "dynamic" (generated per-project/per-user process prose, Jev routing on the hot path, runtime-fetched model guidance) — it is refuted for a five-engineer team by SkillsBench v4's below-baseline result for self-generated skills, by Anthropic's own encoded-preference durability claim, by the per-user-key/fail-open properties of Jev, and by the fact that every other named fix (two skill dirs, disable-model-invocation, folder-map patch, shims, description rewrites, static router block) already has both a measured precedent and existing machinery in this repo.

On the human's position

Q1, "Gates + lifecycle + artifacts fixed; process prose generated": from a team lens the second clause is the problem. "Process prose generated" means five engineers run five processes, and the live SkillsBench v4 result says agent-generated skills land 8–11 pp below having no skill at all, with "confidently wrong pack content" as one named cause. A junior cannot tell confidently wrong from right; that lands on the reviewer. My lens hardens the first clause and flips the second: process prose stays curated and committed (Anthropic's own "encoded preference" category), gets shorter, and gets one static router block. Q2, "Me truly first as I am the super user... if I can get it to work best for me, we can easily get it for others": this is the assumption I would push back on hardest. A harness tuned for a super-user who can recognize slop is exactly the harness that fails the mixed-seniority engineer who cannot; "easily get it for others" is asserted, not evidenced, and no study in the pack compares entry-point counts or onboarding. Q3, "push the new prompting guide to an update and everyone gets the new juice": read literally, this asks for the mechanism Joycraft already has — a versioned update. A team lead wants exactly that (pinned, reproducible, same bytes on every clone via the shared manifest), not a runtime fetch that differs by who ran when. The human's own words argue for the incremental path here. Q4, "in recent sessions I've been getting some slop that took hours and that was not shippable, we have to close that gap": this is the one place my lens agrees the incremental list as written is insufficient — but the fix (a blocking verify step and deterministic checks in the implement loop, committed and identical for all developers) is a sixth incremental item, and the Opus brief's D2 already backlogged it as continuation logic. Q5, "Jev... should be core part of the product now": for a team it cannot be core while it is per-user-key, fail-open, and 99.8% available — those three facts together mean routing is non-deterministic across five machines. My lens moves the human's positions on Q1 (second clause), Q2, Q3 and Q5; it leaves Q4 standing and says it does not require a reimagining to close.

Evidence auditorqualified
Strongest refutation

The two citations that carry the "dynamic" and "22 skills is the problem" halves of P0 do not survive audit, and what remains verified is a bug list that the incremental fixes already cover. (1) SkillsBench: the pack says self-generated skills "provide no benefit on average" (+16.2pp, 86 tasks, 16 of 84 hurt, SE +4.5pp). The live v4 (arxiv.org/html/2602.12670, 2026-06-14) says self-generated skills land BELOW the no-skills baseline, −8.1pp on Claude Code + Opus 4.7 and −11.3pp on Codex + GPT-5.5; curated +16.6pp over 87 tasks; 13 of 87 hurt; SE +11.6pp. Every number is stale and the direction of the generation finding is understated: the primary evidence for on-the-fly generation is negative. (2) Count-sensitivity: issue #64606 (2026-06-02, closed not planned) puts the budget at ~8,000 chars and lists a 22-skill set at 2,801 chars as 35% of budget. Joycraft's 22 descriptions total 3,619 chars (src/skills/*.md, measured) — about 45% of budget. The silent-drop pathology the pack invokes does not occur at Joycraft's size; the "1% of context / least-invoked drop first" sentence is not on the fetched code.claude.com/docs/en/skills page and only appears in third-party posts. (3) The consolidation precedents the pack leans on were incremental: Superpowers deleted stub commands in v5.1.0 (2026-05-04) and dropped its Codex hook in v6.1.0 (2026-06-30) inside its existing architecture; BMAD v6.11.0 (2026-08-10) cut fourteen skills to eight with forwarding shims. Vercel's 100% result (2026-01-27, holds) came from adding an 8KB AGENTS.md index, not from a new harness. (4) Anthropic's own words are subtractive and hedged, not "rebuild": Fable 5 guide says "review and consider removing older instructions"; the skill-creator post (2026-03-03) says capability skills "may become less necessary as models improve. Evals tell you when that's happened" — the pack hardened this to "become unnecessary." (5) Everything I could verify in the repo is on the incremental list: zero skills set disable-model-invocation; the folder map is only rendered through create-once generation (update-inventory.ts:227-262) while tune.md:63 promises upgrade regenerates it; the tune path bug reproduces in generated output (src/codex-skills/joycraft-tune.md:65 → `docs$joycraft-assessment.md`, src/pi-skills/joycraft-tune.md:65 → `docs/skill:joycraft-assessment.md`); 12 of 22 skills exceed 200 lines; three of five installed trees are redundant per §3's path table. None of this needs a reimagining.

Qualification

P0 stands only if, after the incremental fixes plus a single CLI state-query command that closes the 10 verified human-glue handoffs (the one gap the incremental list omits; OpenSpec 1.0.0 is the live precedent), `joycraft telemetry` still shows a measured rate of implement-loop runs ending unshippable. Without that measurement the verified evidence supports the incremental set; the generation pillar is contradicted by SkillsBench v4 (self-generated skills −8.1/−11.3pp below baseline) and the count-sensitivity pillar does not apply at Joycraft's 3,619-char listing.
