Skeptic disagreements

  • Harness ablation (2609.20804) status: novice and ai-researcher mark it 'holds', evidence-auditor 'holds' but says the skeptic angle inverts the cost direction, solo-pi marks it 'misread' on framing (models are open-weight Nemotron/Mistral, not frontier). Numbers hold for all four; the dispute is whether the pack's 'strongest model' framing counts as misreading. I side with solo-pi and the auditor: the pack's frontier inference is not in the paper and the cost direction is opposite to the proposition's skeptic angle.
  • The -53% cost figure: the novice reports it 'not present in my fetch'; the auditor and ai-researcher found it. My fetch confirms it exists verbatim ('reducing cost by 53% and 30%' for bash-only vs predefined tools on Nemotron-3 550B). The novice's unverified item is resolved: the figure holds.
  • Lin et al. tier composition: solo-pi and ai-researcher place GPT-OSS-120B in the mid tier (+15.8pp) alongside Qwen3-235B (+19.3pp); the evidence-auditor places GPT-OSS-120B in the weak tier with Qwen3-32B and concludes 'the inverted-U does not protect open-weight Pi/omp users'. Two of three put GPT-OSS-120B mid-tier, and Qwen3-235B (open-weight, the largest gain) is mid-tier on every reading, so the auditor's conclusion that open-weight equals weak tier overreaches; open-weight models span both tiers.
  • Whether Mistral-Medium-3.5-128B is open-weight: solo-pi calls all four ablation models open-weight; the auditor and ai-researcher say only 'not Claude or GPT'. Mistral Medium has historically been a proprietary API model; I did not verify 3.5's license, so solo-pi's 'all open-weight' is unverified. It does not change the shared point that no frontier closed model was tested.
  • SkillsBench self-generated result: solo-pi and ai-researcher cite the pack's 'no benefit on average'; the auditor fetched the live June 2026 revision and reports self-generated skills 8.1 to 11.3pp BELOW the no-skill baseline on Claude Code + Opus 4.7 and Codex + GPT-5.5. Same direction, different severity; the auditor's live figures should replace the pack's.
  • Skill-creator post: the novice marks it 'dead' (claude.com/blog/skill-creator 404, claim corroborated only by a search snippet, date unconfirmed); the auditor found the live page at claude.com/blog/improving-skill-creator-test-measure-and-refine-agent-skills dated March 3 2026 and marks it 'misread' because the wording is 'may become less necessary as models improve. Evals tell you when that's happened', not 'become unnecessary'. Both are right: the pack's URL is wrong and its paraphrase drops the hedge and the eval gate.
  • What may be cut now without an eval: solo-pi says cut the render blocks, 'Recommended Next Steps' menus, and 'Decide first' paragraphs on every tree; the auditor licenses only trimming new-feature under 500 lines and removing 'Why:' narration; ai-researcher says the first cut is duplication (render block, three research bodies) and nothing else without a measured delta; the novice wants the question-discipline block exempt. The 'Decide first' rule is a decision-first, human-facing presentation rule, so solo-pi's 'cut it as ceremony' sits in tension with the novice's 'keep human-facing discipline inline'.
  • Whether the cut reaches the novice at all: the novice says P8 is invisible to Level 1-2 users (agent-facing prose only) and their real killers are the gates P8 keeps; solo-pi and ai-researcher say the cut actively harms the open-weight path. Different lenses, not a contradiction, but they disagree about whether P8 has any user-facing stakes.
  • Kimi K3's tier: solo-pi flags it may be 'strong' not 'mid' (priced $3/$15 as frontier), ai-researcher calls it near-frontier per press, none can place it on Lin et al.'s curve. All agree it is unverified; only Qwen3-235B is a measured mid-tier proxy.

Citation problems

  • Line counts research 626 / verify 514 / decompose 469 / new-feature 516 and tree total 5,573 are canonical src/skills totals that embed 2-3 harness bodies; the model-facing installed figures are 266/186, 176/174, 436/382, 509/504 and 4,504/4,276. Misread by the pack and the proposition.
  • arXiv 2609.20804 harness ablation: numbers hold, framing does not. Models are Nemotron-3 30B/120B/550B and Mistral-Medium-3.5-128B (no Claude/GPT/Gemini); 'planning' is an update_plan tool plus system protocol, not skill or procedural prose; the pack's 'frontier' inference is not in the paper. The proposition's skeptic angle ('0.4 to 2.0 points, a small penalty for keeping structure') inverts the cost result: planning reduced cost 30-32% on the strongest models. The -53% figure exists (bash-only vs predefined tools, 550B); the novice's 'not found' is resolved.
  • arXiv 2602.12670 SkillsBench: pack cites a stale revision (+16.2pp, 86 tasks, 7,308 trajectories, 16 of 84 hurt, SE +4.5pp, self-generated 'no benefit on average'). Live 2026-06-14 revision: +16.6pp, 87 tasks, 13 of 87 hurt, SE +11.6pp (second lowest), self-generated 8.1-11.3pp below baseline, 'at most three modules'. 7,308 not found.
  • Skill-creator post: pack URL claude.com/blog/skill-creator returns 404; live page is claude.com/blog/improving-skill-creator-test-measure-and-refine-agent-skills (March 3, 2026). Pack paraphrase 'become unnecessary as models improve' drops the hedge and the eval gate: actual wording 'may become less necessary as models improve. Evals tell you when that's happened.'
  • Anthropic Fable 5 guide: pack quotes 'too prescriptive... can degrade output quality' but omits the conditional 'Review and consider removing older instructions if default performance is better.'
  • arXiv 2605.30621 Lin et al.: pack omits tier composition and per-tier numbers; skeptics disagree on whether GPT-OSS-120B is weak or mid tier; the study contains no removal/shortening experiment and does not include Kimi K3.
  • Kimi K3 pricing ($3/$15 per M) rests on secondary sources only (eesel.ai, codersera.com); moonshot.ai primary not fetched.
  • solo-pi's description of all four ablation models as 'open-weight' is unverified for Mistral-Medium-3.5-128B.

What would change the ruling

Flip to keep (cut hard) if a with/without eval on the installed skills, run on Fable 5.1 or Opus 5.5 and on at least one Pi/omp open-weight configuration (Qwen3-235B or kimi-k3 class), shows a non-negative pass-rate or verifier-score delta after removing research's Step 0/isolation/Phase 4 prose and verify's oracle step; that would prove those blocks are dead weight on every tier the one path serves. Flip to a harder keep-the-prose ruling if the same eval shows a measurable loss on the open-weight configuration, or if a study appears that ablates static procedural SKILL.md prose (not a planning tool) on a frontier model and finds harm. Weaken condition (5) if joycraft telemetry shows Pi/omp users overwhelmingly run frontier closed models via API rather than open-weight ones. Drop the novice exemption if P11 rules Levels 1-2 out of scope and Q2's one path is confirmed as practitioners only.

Skeptics

Solo dev on Pi, open-weight modelqualified
Strongest refutation

P8 argues from numbers no model ever reads and from studies that measure something other than skill prose. The "626-line research" and "514-line verify" figures are source files holding three full harness bodies each (src/skills/joycraft-research.md:11,269,448; joycraft-verify.md:12,179,348); the Pi user is served 186 lines (~2.5k tokens) of research and 174 of verify (.pi/skills/*/SKILL.md), both under Claude Code's own 500-line guidance. Only new-feature (504) and decompose (382) are actually long, and in each roughly 60 lines are the same HTML-render ceremony block repeated across six skills (Render and open at .pi/skills/joycraft-research/SKILL.md:104-166, decompose:106-168, new-feature:234-292, design:199-290). Meanwhile the one study that measures benefit from skills-directory content puts my model class at the peak: Qwen3-235B gains +19.3pp on SWE from updated skills versus +2.6pp for Claude Opus 4.6 (arxiv 2605.30621, Table 1, fetched 2026-09-24), and Joycraft's own dogfood profile dispatches Pi on kimi-k3 (AGENTS.md:182). The ablation paper the pack calls "frontier" evidence tested only Nemotron-3 30B/120B/550B and Mistral-Medium — open-weight models — and measured a planning phase, not SKILL.md prose; planning already gave no gain at 120B (arxiv 2609.20804, fetched 2026-09-24). So the two studies disagree about the 200B-1T open-weight class and neither measures the thing P8 wants to cut. Joycraft has zero skill evals on any model (evidence pack §8.6). A hard cut on the Pi tree is therefore a guess, and the guess is made against the tier the only relevant study says benefits most.

Qualification

Cut is safe for this lens only under three conditions. (1) Cut the ceremony, not the protocol: remove the repeated HTML-render blocks, the 'Recommended Next Steps' menus, and the duplicated 'Decide first' paragraphs from every tree (they are handoff-through-human and UI, not scaffolding), but keep the bounded-protocol prose — retrieval caps (3-6 terms, at most 5 files), the isolation subagent prompts, output-path and 'Prior knowledge reused' contracts, and the Phase 4 reconciliation table — in the Pi/omp tree until a mid-tier eval shows they are dead weight. (2) Measure before cutting on Pi: run at least one invocation eval per cut skill on a Qwen3-235B-class model with a BYO key (Joycraft has none today, §8.6); the ablation's 120B null result and the inverted-U's 235B peak conflict for this class, so no cut can be justified from the literature alone. (3) Keep the static prose as the offline, vendor-less default: fetch-and-subtract profiles do not exist for open-weight vendors, so the Pi tree's prose is the only model guidance those users get and must not depend on a network or a Claude-only guide. Also restate the proposition against installed sizes: only new-feature (504) and decompose (382) exceed 300 lines on Pi; research and verify are already compact and should not be named as cut targets.

The prose worth keeping is the prose that caps behaviour (Step 0: 3-6 terms, at most 5 files/rows, 'never block'; the ten-line chat template). .pi/skills/joycraft-research/SKILL.md:8-22 and :104-166 (caps and template); Kimi K3 $3/$15 per M via eesel.ai/blog/kimi-k3-pricing and codersera.com (secondary, 2026), search 2026-09-24

  • Joycraft has no skill evals on any model and no check of which skill ran, so any cut is unmeasured on every tier. docs/research/2026-09-24-dynamic-joycraft-evidence.md §8.6

Evidence against it

  • The ablation shows planning scaffolding stops helping somewhere between 30B and 120B; a Qwen3-235B or Kimi K3 class model is above that, so process scaffolding may already be neutral-to-negative for my own model class. https://arxiv.org/html/2609.20804, fetched 2026-09-24
  • Kimi K3 is priced and marketed as a frontier model ($3/$15), not a bargain mid-tier; my lens's 'mid-tier' assumption may not hold for Kimi, only for Qwen3-235B class. eesel.ai/blog/kimi-k3-pricing, codersera.com/blog/kimi-k3-pricing-api-costs-2026 (secondary), search 2026-09-24
  • Harness-updating quality is flat across tiers (Qwen3.5-9B updates gain about as much as Opus 4.6's), so a mid-tier model generating its own process prose is not the weak link — supports the human's 'process prose generated' if a gate exists. https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.30621, abstract, fetched 2026-09-24
  • About 60 lines per gate skill are HTML-render ceremony identical across six skills, plus 'Recommended Next Steps' menus that hand off through the human; that prose is not what helps a mid-tier model and can be cut on every tier. .pi/skills/joycraft-{research,decompose,new-feature,design}/SKILL.md render blocks; grep count of Render/Next Steps/Decide-first sections across .pi/skills, 2026-09-24
  • Anthropic's checklist advice for unattended runs is still standing instruction plus a to-do file, not step-by-step skill prose, so P8's 'keep persisted state' already covers it. https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/prompting-claude-opus-5-5.md, Unattended agentic runs, fetched 2026-09-24

On the human's position

Q1: "Gates + lifecycle + artifacts fixed; process prose generated." From my lens the generated half has no gate: SkillsBench says self-generated skills give no benefit on average and every study where generation helped had a held-out verifier, and a solo dev on Pi has no held-out task set to be that verifier. The inverted-U does say my model can write updates as good as Opus 4.6's, so generation quality is not the objection — the absence of an acceptance gate for one person on one key is. My lens moves Q1 to: generated prose may exist, but a maintainer-curated static default must ship in the Pi tree and remain the fallback when nothing is generated or accepted. Q3: "push the new prompting guide to an update and everyone gets the new juice." There is no juice for me: r6.2 found no prompting guide from any open-weight vendor, and Codex/Claude Code already inject their own. 'Everyone' in that sentence means Claude and OpenAI users; a Pi/Qwen/Kimi user gets nothing from the fetch path and loses prose if P8 cuts it in the same release. My lens qualifies Q3 to Claude/OpenAI harnesses only. Q4: "Gates that cannot be overridden." I do not fight this — Pi `tool_call` extension hooks can block (evidence pack §7 table), and blocking gates are cheaper for me than prose a mid-tier model follows unevenly. The human's frame is implicitly a Claude Code frame; nothing in Q1-Q4 names the open-weight path the maintainer's own AGENTS.md:182 dispatches to.

Novice vibe coderqualified
Strongest refutation

P8 cuts the part of these four skills I never see and keeps the part that makes me quit. Every line the proposition wants cut is agent-facing; my week-two survival is decided by the questions the skills ask me, and P8 explicitly keeps those as "gates." Concretely, from the named skills: new-feature asks "smoke test budget? lockdown mode desired?" (src/skills/joycraft-new-feature.md:105); decompose asks "Should any of these run in parallel (separate worktrees)?" (joycraft-decompose.md:166), makes me approve "specs 1, 2 → batch; spec 5 → checkpoint; specs 7, 8 → isolated. OK, or adjust?" (:214), and refuses to proceed until I choose Approve / Reword to a traceable source / Drop on every INVENTED premise (:180-186, "never self-approves... human-gated checkpoint on every pass"); verify ends with "N failures need attention. Review the evidence above and fix before proceeding" while forbidding itself to fix them (joycraft-verify.md:150-153, :167) — a report I cannot act on. Research and decompose then end with "Run /clear first" and paste a briefing (joycraft-research.md:231, joycraft-decompose.md:467). None of that is "step-by-step process prose," so cutting the prose changes nothing for me. Worse, the prose that does protect me IS process prose and would go in a "cut hard": "Never dump an unanswerable wall of open prose questions" (new-feature.md:65-67), "Every question has ≥2 real options... 'Defer to <name>' is always a valid answer" (:70-100), and the "Ten lines maximum" chat cap with the repo's own note that pointers do not substitute for inline text ("referenced docs get partially read or skipped at output time... observed live 2026-07-29", :297-299). Second, the headline numbers overstate the cut: 626/514 lines for research/verify are source files holding three near-identical harness variants; the installed Claude skill is 266 and 176 lines, other harnesses 186 and 176 (src/claude-skills, src/pi-skills etc., counted 2026-09-24). Only new-feature (509 installed) and decompose (436) are genuinely long. For research and verify, "cut hard" is mostly a generator dedup that a user on any single harness never experiences. Third, the harness already asks my level and discards it: the brief captures "User expertise: [comfortable / learning / needs guidance]" (new-feature.md:181) and no skill, template, or doc reads that field (grep of src/skills, src/templates, docs/templates: zero consumers).

Qualification

P8 survives for this lens only if (1) the "cut hard" exempts the human-facing question-discipline blocks (new-feature.md:57-100, :285-299) or keeps them inline as a single short paragraph, not a doc pointer — the repo's own note says pointers get skipped; and (2) the proposition is restated against installed sizes (research 266/186, verify 176, new-feature 509, decompose 436), so that "which skills die" is answered for new-feature and decompose, where the length is real, and not credited for research and verify, where most of the 626/514 is a three-way harness fork. Under those two conditions the cut is invisible to a novice — it neither helps nor hurts week-two retention — and the novice's actual killers (decompose's gates, verify's unactionable verdict, /clear handoffs) remain P3/P9/P11 problems that P8 does not touch.

Evidence for the refutation

  • Two of the four named line counts are harness duplication, not process depth: research 626 source → 266 (Claude) / 186 (Codex, Pi, Copilot, omp) installed; verify 514 → 176/174. new-feature 516 → 509 and decompose 469 → 436 are the genuinely long ones. wc -l on src/skills/*.md and src/{claude,codex,pi,copilot,omp}-skills/joycraft-{research,verify,decompose,new-feature}.md, 2026-09-24; variant markers at src/skills/joycraft-research.md:3,269,448 and joycraft-verify.md:3,179,348

Evidence against it

  • Anthropic says a brief instruction now steers most behaviors without enumerating each case, so the novice-protecting question discipline could shrink to one paragraph rather than being cut or kept whole. https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/prompting-claude-fable-5.md, 'Strong instruction following' and 'Refactor existing prompts and skills' sections, fetched 2026-09-24

  • Anthropic's checklist recommendation for unattended Opus 5.5 is persisted state ('a to-do tool or a file'), which P8 keeps; it is not an argument for step-by-step skill prose. https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/prompting-claude-opus-5-5.md, 'Unattended agentic runs', fetched 2026-09-24
  • The inverted-U argument does not bite for this lens: a Level 1-2 user does not pick a model and runs the harness default, which on Claude Code is a frontier model; mid-tier/open-weight benefit is the Pi/omp lens's fight. https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.30621 (mid-tier benefit most, strong-tier less), fetched 2026-09-24; default-model claim UNVERIFIED
  • Anthropic's own taxonomy says workflow-sequencing ('encoded preference') skills persist while capability-uplift skills die, so cutting process prose does not by itself kill the four skills as workflows. https://claude.com/blog/improving-skill-creator-test-measure-and-refine-agent-skills (via WebSearch snippet, 2026-09-24)

On the human's position

Q1: "Gates + lifecycle + artifacts fixed; process prose generated... getting people used to TDD agentic development as opposed to endless vibe coding (the essence and core objective of joycraft)." From my lens this is backwards. The gates are the only part of these four skills I ever touch, and they are the part I cannot pass: I do not know what a smoke test budget, a worktree, an execution mode, or an INVENTED premise is, and verify's "fix before proceeding" is a wall. Fixing the gates and regenerating the prose I never read locks in the exact surface that ends my week two. "Getting people used to TDD" reads as a question I cannot answer unless the gate carries a pre-selected recommendation and an "I don't know, pick for me" answer; the maintainer already proposed that escape under P9, but Q1 does not extend it to the gates. Q4: "Gates that cannot be overridden" — an unoverridable INVENTED gate in front of a novice is an abandonment, not a safeguard. Q2: "Me truly first as the super user... 15 colleagues... one path." If the one path is tuned to someone who reads diffs, my lens does not move Q1 at all — I am simply not a user, and P8 stands for me trivially because nothing in it reaches me. My lens moves Q1 only if novices are in scope (Q7 added my lens; P11 asks whether Levels 1-2 are the market): then the condition is that the "fixed" gates get novice-safe defaults (recommendation pre-picked, defer/"pick for me" first-class, verify defaulting to "fix it for me"), and that the question-discipline prose in new-feature.md:57-100 and :285-299 is exempted from the cut or kept inline as one short paragraph rather than a pointer. Cheap first step either way: read the "User expertise" field the brief already captures (new-feature.md:181) instead of discarding it.

AI researcherqualified
Strongest refutation

P8 rests on no measurement of the thing it proposes, and its premise miscounts the thing it wants to cut. (1) The line counts are source totals across three harness variants: a user on any one harness receives research at 266 lines (Claude) or 186 (Codex/Pi/Copilot/omp), and verify at 176 everywhere (src/research-skill variants at src/skills/joycraft-research.md:11-268, 269-447, 448-626; generated files src/claude-skills/ and src/pi-skills/). Verify as delivered is already under Joycraft's own 200-line skill threshold (src/skills/joycraft-optimize.md:110). (2) Neither cited paper measured removing procedural prose from a strong model. The harness ablation (arXiv 2609.20804) ablated an update_plan tool plus a system-protocol on Nemotron-3 30B/120B/550B and Mistral-Medium-3.5-128B, never a Claude or GPT-6 model, never a SKILL.md; its strong-tier finding is "planning shifts to a cost saver ... with little change in accuracy" — a reason to keep structure at the top tier, not cut it. Lin et al. (arXiv 2605.30621) report strong-tier gains of +2.6pp (Opus 4.6) and +2.8pp (Sonnet 4.6) from evolved skills — smaller than mid-tier (+15.8 to +19.3pp) but still gains — and the paper "contains no experiments removing or shortening procedural instructions for strong models." The inverted-U says frontier models benefit less; P8 reads it as harm. (3) The one vendor statement of harm is conditional: Anthropic's Fable 5 guide says prior-model skills are "often too prescriptive ... Review and consider removing older instructions if default performance is better" — i.e., measure first — and the same page and the Opus 5.5 page add scaffolding (checklist the model updates, fresh-context verifier subagents, grounded progress claims, a memory system, an autonomous-run reminder). (4) P8 is internally inconsistent: roughly 60% of verify's delivered body is the verifier prompt, the oracle-gathering step, and the report contract (src/skills/joycraft-verify.md:34-49, 64-127, 128-158) — the "independent verification" P8 says to keep. Research's "process" is an information-flow constraint ("the researching agent must never see the brief," :12; Phase 4 reconciliation added after a documented drift incident, :147-167), not stay-on-task filler; capability does not remove the need for isolation. (5) Joycraft has no in-product delta: the level5-skill-evals brief is still DRAFT (docs/features/2026-04-07-level5-skill-evals-draft/brief.md:4), check.sh cannot tell which skill ran (pack §8.6), and Compound Engineering's ce-retune refuses to retune without an A/B harness (pack §5.6) — a standard P8 does not meet.

Qualification

P8 survives only as: subtractive edits to the delivered per-harness skill bodies (not the source totals), made one skill at a time, each kept only if a measured pass-rate or verifier-score delta is non-negative on every model class Joycraft's one path serves (frontier Claude/GPT-6, plus the open-weight model Pi/omp users run, e.g. kimi-k3 per AGENTS.md:182), using the eval Anthropic ships (`claude plugin eval`, baseline-vs-plugin Δ over 3 runs) or a `pi -p` equivalent. Excluded from any cut regardless of delta: research's brief-isolation rule and Phase 4 reconciliation, verify's oracle gathering and verifier prompt, and the decision gates — these are information-flow constraints, not stay-on-task scaffolding, and no cited paper measured removing them. The first cut should be duplication, not process: the 45-line render block copied into 7 skills and the three full-body research variants that differ only by subagent mechanics (197 diff lines between Claude and Codex variants, 4 between Codex and Pi).

On the human's position

Q1 says the invariant is 'Gates + lifecycle + artifacts fixed; process prose generated', with 'the formality of the loop' and 'getting people used to TDD agentic development' named as the biggest wins. Two problems from my lens. First, 'generated' process prose is the one configuration the literature measured and found null: SkillsBench's self-generated skills 'provide no benefit on average' (pack §4.1), and Lin et al. show even Opus 4.6's evolved skills gain only +2.6pp — so the human's proposed replacement for the cut prose has weaker evidence than the prose it replaces. Second, 'the formality of the loop' is process prose: the loop's formality lives in research's isolation rule (:12), verify's oracle step (:34-49), and decompose's decision gate — cut those and the formality goes with them. Q4 moves my verdict harder: 'in recent sessions I've been getting some slop that took hours and that was not shippable' — this happened on Opus 5.5 / Fable 5.1 with today's prose intact. That is the human's own observation that frontier capability plus current scaffolding still produces slop; nothing in P8's cut addresses it, and the human's own diagnosis (Helix, 'gates that cannot be overridden') points at verification, not at excess instruction. The human's Q3 hope — 'push the new prompting guide to an update and everyone gets the new juice' — assumes vendor guidance is additive; the live Fable 5 page says the opposite: remove instructions only 'if default performance is better', which requires an eval the product does not have. Q2 ('one path' for fifteen colleagues 'across different size teams') plus AGENTS.md:182 (Pi on kimi-k3, open-weight) means any cut is applied to the model class the inverted-U says benefits 6-7x more than the frontier tier. My lens does not move the human off subtraction as a direction; it moves them off 'cut hard' as a method and off 'generated' as the replacement. The condition is a per-skill, per-model-class A/B — `claude plugin eval` (v2.1.269) or a `pi -p` equivalent — with the cut kept only where the delta is non-negative on every model the one path serves.

Strongest refutation

P8 rests on numbers that are misread and on studies that do not test its premise. (1) The line counts are canonical source files that embed two or three full per-harness bodies. Installed, what a model reads is: research 266 lines on Claude / 186 on Pi, Codex, omp, Copilot (not 626); verify 176 / 174 (not 514); decompose 436 / 382; new-feature 509 / 504 (src/claude-skills/, src/pi-skills/, wc -l 2026-09-24). Research is overstated 2.4x, verify 2.9x. Of verify's 176 installed lines, ~70 are the read-only verifier-subagent prompt (src/claude-skills/joycraft-verify.md:64-127), which is the "independent verification" the proposition says to keep; verify is not process prose. (2) No cited study measures static hand-written process prose on a frontier Claude or GPT-6 model. The harness ablation (arXiv 2609.20804) tests Nemotron-3 30B/120B/550B and Mistral-Medium-3.5; its "strongest" is a 550B Nemotron. And its cost figure runs the other way from the skeptic angle: for the 550B model, enabling planning cut cost ~30-32% with -2.0/-0.4pp accuracy, so keeping the planning scaffold is net cheaper, not "a small penalty." Lin et al. (2605.30621) measures benefit from self-evolved harness updates, not static prose; its weak tier is the open-weight models (Qwen3-32B, GPT-OSS-120B) and they "gain little," so the inverted-U does not protect open-weight Pi/omp users the way the angle claims. (3) SkillsBench (2602.12670), cited from a stale revision, in its live June 2026 version still shows curated skills adding +18.2 to +24.8pp on Claude Code + Opus 4.7, Codex + GPT-5.5, and Gemini CLI + Gemini 3.1 Pro, and self-generated skills landing 8.1 to 11.3pp BELOW the no-skill baseline. The one live datum that supports cutting is the same paper's "compact and standard-length Skills (+19.0, +21.5pp) outperform detailed (+14.5) and comprehensive documentation (+0.7)", which argues for shorter, de-narrated skills, not for removing step structure because frontier models no longer need it. Anthropic's own sentence is conditional: "Review and consider removing older instructions if default performance is better" (Fable 5 guide, fetched 2026-09-24). The evidence supports shorten-and-measure, not "cut hard."

Qualification

P8 stands only under three conditions. (1) It is re-stated against installed variants (research 266/186, verify 176/174, decompose 436/382, new-feature 509/504), not canonical source; the source-level duplication is a maintainer cost, not a model-facing one, and belongs to a different proposition. (2) verify is removed from the cut list and research's Step 0 retrieval and question/fact isolation (src/claude-skills/joycraft-research.md:16-32, 78-82) are classed as verification structure, not process prose. (3) Every cut ships behind a with/without eval on the actual harness + model pairs Joycraft serves, including at least one Pi or omp open-weight configuration, in the SkillsBench pattern; the only live evidence for cutting is 'compact beats comprehensive' plus a vendor sentence conditioned on 'if default performance is better.' What the evidence does license now, without an eval: trim new-feature under the documented 500-line limit and remove 'Why:' narration per 'state what to do rather than narrating how or why.'

On the human's position

Q1: \"biggest wins in addition is the STE (Simplified Technical English) language directive, the formality of the loop, getting people used to TDD agentic development\" with the choice \"Gates + lifecycle + artifacts fixed; process prose generated.\" Two audit problems. First, \"formality of the loop\" and \"process prose\" are not separable in the files: decompose's loop formality is its step rules (3-7 specs, one-sentence descriptions, ≤2 dependencies, src/claude-skills/joycraft-decompose.md:77-90) and verify's is a 70-line verifier prompt. Cutting prose hard while keeping formality is not a choice the current files permit without naming which lines are which. Second, \"process prose generated\" is the one configuration with measured harm in the live evidence: SkillsBench's current revision puts self-generated skills 8.1 to 11.3pp below the no-skill baseline on Claude Code + Opus 4.7 and Codex + GPT-5.5, worse than the pack's \"no benefit on average.\" My lens moves \"generated\" to \"curated, shortened, and eval-gated\"; it does not move the invariant (gates, artifacts, STE, TDD), which no citation contradicts. Q3: \"push the new prompting guide to an update and everyone gets the new juice\" skips the condition the guide itself attaches, \"if default performance is better\", and the skill-creator post's \"Evals tell you when that's happened.\" The vendor asks for a measurement before removal; a push without one is the same untested prior the proposition rests on.

P9 · 4 skeptics

Front-loaded quality at the design bookend

qualify
Ruling

P9 stands only in its subtractive, human-declared form: a readiness state the human declares (never the agent infers) that keeps exploration in chat and renders the checkpoint once the human says the idea is clear; a first-class "I don't know yet / explore this" escape in the existing checkpoint that records an open row with an owner and returns to chat, never auto-routing to a panel; and visuals (mockups for frontend, inline diagrams for complex API/database work) drawn inside the existing design and review-gate renders under the one-template rule, tiered by the human-approved risk judgment that already exists. Panels as a standard per-feature step, new diagram or prototype templates, and any agent-side clarity detector do not stand: they have zero external evidence, zero cost measurement, zero skill mechanism, and their one external anchor (Helix) does not describe them.

The claim as argued

Panels while exploring, checkpoint artifacts once the idea is clear (switch on clarity, not on skill boundary; "I do not know yet" as a valid answer), diagrams and prototypes before specs, all tiered by risk, so spec and implementation tokens land on what the human wants. The maintainer runs panels and prototypes by hand today and reports it works. Skeptic angles: cost of a panel per feature; artifact fatigue (the reading-fatigue verdict was delete, tier, verify); prototype and spec drift; how the agent detects clarity; whether a novice can use any of it.

Replacement claim

Front-load quality at the design bookend by switching surface on human-declared clarity, not on skill boundary: chat (and hand-run panels, at the human's call) while exploring; the existing checkpoint, with an "I don't know yet" escape that records an owned open row, once the human declares the idea clear; visuals inside the existing gate renders, tiered by the human-approved risk judgment. Panels, diagram templates and prototypes remain human-decided practice, not shipped standard steps, until a panel's cost is measured and the checkpoint works on every harness.

Condition

P9 holds when all of the following are true: (a) clarity is a human-declared state ("still exploring" vs "ready to decide"), added as one sentence to the shared question directive in the eight gate skills, identical across harnesses; while the human says they are exploring, stay in chat and render no checkpoint; no agent-side inference. (b) The checkpoint gains a fourth escape (`__explore`) that leaves the question `open` with an owner (default the answerer) and a revisit gate, returns to chat, and never auto-routes to a panel; this touches CHECKPOINT_TEMPLATE.html, interactive-checkpoint.md, decide.md's terminal states, the five PRE_PRESENTATION skills and gate-contract tests once. (c) The dossier pilot's kill criterion is adjudicated on the record before anything is called standard: count bypasses since 2026-07-20 and stamp the re-reading "bypass while exploring is expected; bypass once declared clear kills the format". (d) Visuals stay inside existing renders (design.html, review-gate, checkpoint) as inline SVG or mockup under D1's one-template rule; mockups for frontend features are the first visual, sequence/data-flow diagrams only when the existing human-approved risk judgment marks the feature complex. Excluded until preconditions are met: panels as a per-feature step (preconditions: token and hour cost measured on at least two features, one before/after on rework or parked-after-approval), new diagram/prototype templates and any prototype without a reconciliation step to the spec (precondition: the non-Claude checkpoint server ships so ceremony is not paste-back on four harnesses), automated risk tiering beyond the existing human-approved mode heuristic.

Judge's reasoning

All four skeptics returned "qualified"; none argued keep or flip, and their qualifications overlap on the core. What is repo-verified and uncontested: interview.md:39 and :44 force a checkpoint page for any gate with two or more questions with no clarity condition, on every harness; the escape set is __backlog/__discard/__defer only (CHECKPOINT_TEMPLATE.html:264-268, interactive-checkpoint.md:31); the read-back already knows an `open` state for unanswered questions, so a fourth escape is a small extension, not new machinery. The timing defect the maintainer names is therefore real and cheap to fix, and it sits inside the reading-fatigue verdict rather than against it: RF-DIET-3 endorses a decision-forcing checkpoint at design and RF-DIET-2 says a doc enters the human channel only if it requires a decision. That is why this is not a flip.

What does not survive: the additive half. (1) Panels: zero hits for "panel" in src/skills; no token or hour cost recorded for any panel run (3, 13, 52, ~50 agents); Helix, verified live, has no pre-code design, diagram, prototype or panel phase — the engineer approves a checkpoint sequence "in minutes" and then reviews "the code and running app", so it supports early feedback on working code (Q4/P3), not pre-spec ceremony. (2) Prototypes/diagrams as templates: succinct-gates D1 (decision-log:70) chose one generic template because per-gate templates multiply render checks; install-manifest.ts:30 has no ownership kind for agent-generated files. (3) Agent-detected clarity: no eval, no check, no precedent; decision-log 2026-05-30 kept mode selection human-approved because "only a human knows" risk. (4) The existing front-loaded gate is already skipped: 60 folders, 47 briefs, 10 design.md, 13 of 23 spec'd features with no design.md; one committed checkpoint render; and the Opus 5.5 feature went through two checkpoints, brief approval (D9) and nine specs and was parked the same day (2026-09-24, commits a9565e0/1d30997). That last fact cuts both ways: implementation tokens were saved, spec tokens were not; it is weak evidence for the bookend and strong evidence that more pre-spec artifacts do not by themselves make spec tokens land.

The Deposition Checkpoint pilot's kill criterion ("kill the format if Max bypasses the questions into free chat by the second feature", decision-dossier brief.md:88-90) was never adjudicated: decision-log 2026-09-23 C3 extended checkpoints to all eight gate skills, but no row records the pilot surviving. The evidence pack's own origin line is a bypass. The maintainer's clarification resolves the contradiction only if the criterion is re-read on the record as "bypass while exploring is expected; bypass once declared clear kills the format". That re-reading is a condition of this ruling, not an assumption.

On Q2's transfer claim ("if I can get it to work best for me, we can easily get it for others"): the checkpoint the maintainer calls amazing is the db-published Claude page; on Codex, Pi, omp and Copilot it is a paste-back block (interactive-checkpoint.md local mode; backlog 2026-09-23), which is RF-KILL-6. The team-lead and maintainer lenses are right that the super-user's experience does not transfer until the local server ships, so every added ceremony lands on four harnesses as a killed pattern.

Strongest refutation considered

The evidence-auditor's: P9 has no external evidence, its one anchor (Helix) is misread, the existing design gate is skipped in 13 of 23 spec'd features, the only fully front-loaded feature (Opus 5.5) was parked the day it was approved, and the Q4 slop sessions happened with design, decide and checkpoint already shipped, so the existing front-loaded gates did not prevent the failure the maintainer wants fixed. I verified Helix live and the auditor is right: the engineer approves a checkpoint sequence "in minutes" and reviews "the code and running app"; there is no pre-code design, diagram, prototype or panel step. This kills the additive half of P9 and reassigns the Q4 motive to P3 (blocking gates in the implement loop). It does not flip P9 because the timing defect is repo-verified (interview.md:39,44; three fixed escapes), the reading-fatigue verdict itself endorses a decision-forcing design checkpoint (RF-DIET-3), and the stated first customer (Q2) reports the clear-idea checkpoint works, with nine decisions stamped through one page in a day. The Opus 5.5 parking is also ambiguous: it wasted spec tokens but saved implementation tokens, which is half of what P9 promises.

Human position moved?

Yes, on four of the five positions, with evidence. (1) The P9 clarification's 'switch on clarity' is strengthened but reshaped: all four skeptics converge that the human declares clarity and the agent never infers it; the clarification's 'human or the agent signals' loses its agent half because no eval, check or precedent exists (evidence pack line 211; decision-log 2026-05-30 'only a human knows'). The maintainer's own behavior supports the human-declared version: Q8 ('no brief though, as you and I will have follow up discussion') and the pack's chat-only origin are consistent with a person who knows when he is exploring. (2) 'I don't know yet routes back to chat or to a panel' is moved: routing an unclear answer to a panel is rejected by the novice (a 41-53 KB adversarial document is unreadable for that user) and by the maintainer lens (no panel mechanism, no cost); routing to chat alone is rejected by the team-lead (chat has no owner, and the repo already solved this with defer-to-person D2/D11). The panel converges on an owned open row that returns to chat. (3) 'Panels as a standard step' is moved to not-standard: zero cost figures across 3-, 13-, 52- and ~50-agent panels, zero skill mechanism, Helix misread (verified live: no pre-code panel), and the Opus 5.5 feature approved and parked the same day after full front-loading. The maintainer's hand-run practice stays exactly as it is; the panel denies only that it should ship as ceremony. (4) 'More visuals' is split: component mockups and prototypes survive as the one surface that needs no reading (novice, Helix's early-feedback principle applied to something a person can look at), but sequence and data-flow diagrams stay inside existing renders under D1's one-template rule and behind the risk judgment; new templates and untethered prototypes fail on drift (design.md:185-192) and on the manifest gap (install-manifest.ts:30). (5) Q2's 'if I can get it to work best for me, we can easily get it for others' is moved for the checkpoint specifically: the 'amazing' page is the Claude db-published page; on Codex, Pi, omp and Copilot it is paste-back (RF-KILL-6), so the transfer waits on the backlogged server. Not moved: Q1 (formality of the loop, TDD as the core objective) — every skeptic keeps the decision-forcing checkpoint at design, and RF-DIET-3 endorses it. Reframed: Q4's slop gap ('hours of unshippable output') happened with design, decide and the checkpoint already shipped, so it is evidence for P3's implement-loop gates, Helix's actual mechanism, not for more design-bookend ceremony; P9 does not close the Q4 gap.

Skeptic disagreements

  • Destination of 'I don't know yet': novice says chat or another prototype iteration and never a panel; team-lead says never chat because chat has no owner, make it a committed open row with owner and revisit gate (extending __defer); maintainer says an 'explore' escape that leaves the question open and returns to chat; evidence-auditor names the escape but no destination. Ruling adopts the team-lead's owned open row with the maintainer's return-to-chat, and the novice's ban on auto-routing to a panel.
  • Who signals clarity: team-lead says a human-declared state recorded in the gate, never inferred; maintainer says the human, not the agent; novice says a novice cannot declare clarity and the only working signal is a reaction to a prototype; evidence-auditor cites the Fable 5 guide ('pause only when the work requires them') without a mechanism. All four reject agent inference; they differ on whether a novice can declare at all.
  • Diagrams: novice says sequence and data-flow diagrams do not survive for Level 1-2 users and belong behind the P11 fork; evidence-auditor accepts risk-tiered diagrams inside the existing design gate; maintainer allows inline SVG in existing renders only, under D1's one-template rule; team-lead wants them opted in per risk tier by a committed AGENTS.md policy line.
  • Prototypes: novice says a clickable mockup is the one P9 surface that survives and should be the first artifact a novice meets; maintainer excludes prototype templates entirely until the non-Claude server ships and a panel cost exists; team-lead accepts throwaway prototypes only with a reconciliation step to the spec like design Step 3; evidence-auditor puts them in a pilot with instrumentation.
  • Helix citation: novice, team-lead and maintainer mark it 'holds' (quotes verbatim, with the team-lead and maintainer noting the extension to pre-spec artifacts is a stretch); evidence-auditor marks it 'misread'. Judge's live check agrees with the auditor: the text holds, the use as support for pre-spec design artifacts does not.
  • Panels' path to standard: novice gates them behind P11 or explicit request; team-lead wants one team feature's panel priced in tokens and hours and a per-tier AGENTS.md policy; maintainer keeps them hand-run and human-decided until cost is measured on two features; evidence-auditor demands a pilot with bypass/skip telemetry, per-panel token cost and a before/after. All agree they are not standard today.
  • The bypass-to-chat kill criterion: maintainer re-reads it as 'bypass while unclear is expected; bypass once clear kills' and wants it stamped; evidence-auditor says the brainstorm-mode 'hindrance' is the July kill signal reframed after an uninstrumented graduation; team-lead wants bypasses counted before any re-reading; novice notes the super-user bypassed in the very session that produced P9.
  • Feature-folder count since 2026-07-20: team-lead reports 13; the judge's glob over 2026-07/08/09 returns 15 (includes early-July folders). Not material to the ruling.
  • Whether P9 is even about its stated first customer: novice says the proposition is out of scope for Q2's maintainer-first frame and only constrains shape; team-lead says Q2's 'works for me then for others' is exactly the transfer that fails on a mixed-harness team.

Citation problems

  • Shopify Helix (shopify.engineering/helix): every quoted sentence holds verbatim, but its use in section 9 item 8 as support for pre-spec panels/diagrams/prototypes is a misread. Verified live by the judge: the only pre-code human step is approving a checkpoint sequence 'in minutes'; the engineer then reviews 'the code and running app'. Helix supports P3/Q4 (gates on implemented checkpoints), not P9's design-bookend ceremony. Three skeptics marked it 'holds'; the evidence-auditor's 'misread' is correct.
  • docs/guides/levels.md:24 'Most developers plateau at Level 2' misreads Dan Shapiro's five-levels post, which says 'almost everyone tops out here' about Level 3 (novice lens, live fetch 2026-09-24). Not a direct P9 citation but it anchors the novice framing.
  • arXiv 2609.00252 cited as 'no controlled study of spec-driven development exists': directionally right, wording overstated; the paper says the evidence base is immature and is a conceptual first step; the words 'controlled', 'empirical', 'experiment' do not appear (evidence-auditor).
  • Skill-creator post: the pack-implied URL claude.com/blog/skill-creator returns 404; the live post is claude.com/blog/improving-skill-creator-test-measure-and-refine-agent-skills (2026-03-03); substance holds as paraphrase (evidence-auditor).
  • Agent OS v3.0.0 release year: pack says 2026-01-20; a fetch summary printed 2025; day/month match, year unverified (evidence-auditor).
  • P9 paraphrases the reading-fatigue verdict as 'ask the human for decisions instead of reading'; the source reads 'demand decisions instead of reading' and 'kill if you bypass to chat'. Holds in substance.
  • Team-lead's tally '13 feature folders since 2026-07-20': the judge's glob over 2026-07/08/09 returns 15 (includes early-July folders). Immaterial.

What would change the ruling

Toward keep (panels and prototypes as standard, risk-tiered steps): a recorded token and wall-clock cost for a panel on at least two features; a before/after showing that features that passed a panel or prototype had lower rework or fewer parked-after-approval outcomes than features that did not; the non-Claude checkpoint server shipped so the deciding surface is the same on every harness; and telemetry showing the clarity-declared checkpoint is completed, not bypassed, once the human declares clarity. Toward flip (drop the design-bookend additions and move the effort to P3): telemetry showing checkpoints are still bypassed after the clarity switch ships, or the `__explore` escape used as a permanent dodge on most questions, or the design-gate skip rate staying near 13 of 23 after the change; or a controlled study finding that upfront design artifacts do not reduce agent rework. A vendor or independent measurement that an agent can detect idea clarity reliably would reopen the agent-inference half that this ruling excludes.

Skeptics

Novice vibe coderqualified
Strongest refutation

P9's own escape hatch routes the least capable user into the least usable surface. The proposition says "I do not know yet / explore this" should route "back to chat or to a panel" (evidence pack line 254). A panel in this repo produces 41-53 KB adversarial documents with citations (docs/research/2026-09-24-dynamic-joycraft-evidence.md 52,711 bytes; docs/research/2026-07-20-reading-fatigue-brief.html 52,455 bytes; the checkpoint page itself 41,455 bytes) built by 8 research agents plus 7 skeptic lenses plus judges (pack line 10, lines 262-263) or a "13-agent panel" (docs/context/decision-log.md:36). A person who cannot read a diff cannot read that, and cannot judge whether the panel's verdict is right. So for me, "I don't know" leads to a wall of text, then to a checkpoint whose every question demands a typed "<choice> because <reason>" (src/skills/joycraft-interview.md:48-56; docs/templates/CHECKPOINT_TEMPLATE.html:243) and whose only escapes are Backlog, Discard, or Defer to a named person (CHECKPOINT_TEMPLATE.html:264-267; a solo novice has nobody to defer to, and an unnamed defer is refused, interview.md:57-60). Second, the reading-fatigue verdict P9 must clear was "delete nominal output, tier the channels, retrieve just-in-time, and demand decisions instead of reading" (reading-fatigue-brief.html:229); P9 adds three artifact classes (panel reports, diagrams, prototypes) before the spec even exists. Third, the Deposition Checkpoint pilot's kill criterion was "kill if you bypass to chat" (reading-fatigue-brief.html:486), and the super-user bypassed to chat in the very session that produced P9: "Origin: /joycraft-interview session (chat-only, no gate artifacts by request)" (pack line 6). If the maintainer opts out of the artifact when exploring, a novice never opens it. Fourth, "the agent detects clarity" has no measurement anywhere in the repo: there are no invocation or behavior evals and check.sh cannot even tell which skill ran (pack line 211), so a clarity gate ships as unmeasured prose, the very thing the synthesis says to cut (pack line 224). What survives my lens: prototypes and component mockups before specs. A novice can look at a screen and say "not like that"; that is the one P9 surface that needs no reading and no vocabulary, and Helix's "moves feedback to the earliest useful point" (live, shopify.engineering/helix, 2026-09-21) applies to it. Sequence and data-flow diagrams do not survive: a Level 1-2 person cannot read a sequence diagram any more than a diff.

Qualification

P9 stands for this lens only under this condition: the default surface while exploring is chat, the first artifact a novice meets is a clickable mockup or prototype (frontend) or a plain-language "here is what I think you want" page (backend), the checkpoint gains an "I don't know yet" escape that routes to chat or to another prototype iteration and never to a panel, and panels plus sequence/data-flow diagrams are gated behind the practitioner fork (P11) or an explicit request. Any version where panels and diagrams are "standard steps" for every user, or where the checkpoint still requires a typed rationale with only Backlog/Discard/Defer escapes, fails week-two retention for a Level 1-2 user. The proposition is also out of scope for its stated first customer (Q2: maintainer first), so this qualification constrains the shape of P9, not whether the maintainer should build it for himself.

Unverified

  • Dollar or token cost of one panel per feature: no cost record exists in the repo; only agent counts and output byte sizes are measurable.
  • Whether any Level 1-2 user has ever used Joycraft: no user-level telemetry exists; the 15 daily colleagues' skill levels are the maintainer's report only (pack line 262).
  • Whether an agent can detect idea clarity reliably: no eval, study, or prior-art measurement was found in the pack or the repo.
  • Whether the checkpoint page is usable on non-Claude harnesses by someone who cannot paste a JSON block correctly: inferred from decide.md:164-168, not tested.

On the human's position

The human's words: "the artifacts are not the problem — answering questions directly inside them is 'amazing' once the idea is clear"; "the switch should key on clarity, not on which skill is running"; "'I don't know yet / explore this' as a first-class answer ... that routes back to chat or to a panel"; "artifacts need more visuals — sequence and data-flow diagrams ... component mockups and prototypes" (pack line 254). And on the customer: "Me truly first as I am the super user ... 15 colleagues ... one path ... as this system gets much easier ... this becomes a non issue really" (Q2). From my lens: the clarity switch is right in direction but the human answered only half of it. Clarity is something the super-user can feel and signal; I cannot. I do not know whether my idea is clear until I see it, so for me the only working clarity signal is a prototype I react to, not a question I answer. "I don't know" as a first-class answer is the one change that stops me abandoning at the checkpoint, but only if it routes to chat or to a mockup, never to a panel, because a panel's output is the wall of text I cannot read. The diagram half of "more visuals" does not move for me at all: sequence diagrams are a practitioner surface (P10/P11 fork), and mockups are the novice surface. The "amazing" claim is real but it is the super-user's testimony about an artifact tuned for him after two months of pilots, and he himself ran this exploration chat-only, which is the exact kill criterion his own panel set. The Q2 frame ("one path", maintainer first) means my lens does not flip P9; the human has already said the novice is not the first customer. It does move P9's shape: if "one path" is serious, the path must default to chat-plus-mockup and unlock panels, diagrams, and rationale-required checkpoints only when the user or a P11 profile asks for them. As written, with panels and diagrams standard and the checkpoint's escapes unchanged, I am gone before week two, and "TDD agentic development as the core objective" (Q1) never gets a chance to teach me anything.

Team lead, five engineersqualified
Strongest refutation

As a *standard* step for a five-developer team, P9 fails on consistency before it can deliver quality. (1) The artifact that "dialogues with the user" is two different products on a mixed team: on Claude the answers live in one developer's private artifact store and never in the file (docs/templates/reference/interactive-checkpoint.md:16); on Codex/Copilot/Pi the same gate is a local page whose answers the developer pastes back as a block (interactive-checkpoint.md:5, :46-50; docs/backlog/2026-09-23-checkpoint-non-claude-harnesses.md). Only the stamped `decisions:` rows reach the repo, so the design-bookend record is already per-developer, and P9 adds three more artifact kinds (panel verdicts, diagrams, prototypes) with no committed home or reconciliation. (2) "Switch on clarity" pushes the biggest source of variance into the least observable variable. Nothing in the repo detects clarity; every gate skill forces a checkpoint page at two or more questions regardless (src/skills/joycraft-interview.md:39,44; joycraft-design.md:125,132; joycraft-new-feature.md:61,68). Five engineers have five clarity thresholds: a junior signals "clear" early because they do not know what they do not know, a senior signals late; the lead cannot see either. The checkpoint template has no "I do not know" escape at all today, only `__backlog`, `__discard`, `__defer` (interactive-checkpoint.md:31; docs/templates/CHECKPOINT_TEMPLATE.html:267), and routing an unknown "back to chat" would destroy the one thing a team record needs: an owner. (3) The format P9 extends already tripped its own kill criterion and nobody adjudicated it. The Deposition Checkpoint shipped as a pilot: "Kill the format if Max bypasses the questions into free chat by the second feature" (docs/features/2026-07-20-decision-dossier/brief.md:89-92; docs/features/2026-07-20-reading-fatigue-panel/research.md:47-49). The evidence pack's own origin line is "chat-only, no gate artifacts by request" (docs/research/2026-09-24-dynamic-joycraft-evidence.md:5), the maintainer calls the artifact "a hindrance" in brainstorm mode (:254), and across 13 feature folders since 2026-07-20 there is exactly one rendered checkpoint, 7 dossiers, 6 design.md files and 4 briefs with zero `decisions:` rows (ls/grep tally, docs/features/). No pilot review exists in decision-log.md, shipped.md or discoveries/. Building diagrams and prototypes on top of an unadjudicated kill is how a team lead ends up normalizing five different ceremonies by hand. (4) Prototype/spec drift is unhandled. The design skill already needs a whole reconciliation step because brief and design silently diverged once ("11 clean / 9 dirty", joycraft-design.md:185-192). A pre-spec prototype is a third artifact with no such step; on a team, dev A's HTML mockup becomes the de facto spec dev B implements differently, and a novice ships the prototype. (5) Panel cost is unmeasured anywhere: Helix publishes no cost or adoption numbers (live check) and describes code-level checkpoints after design, not pre-spec panels or prototypes, so the pack's Helix quote supports "early feedback" but not this mechanism. Panel output is LLM prose, and RF-5 says polished LLM plans "invite acknowledgment, not scrutiny" (research.md RF-5); five persuasive verdicts per week is added review load for the lead, not less.

Qualification

P9 stands only under all of: (a) the clarity switch is a human-declared state ('still exploring' vs 'ready to decide') recorded in the gate, never inferred by the agent, and the same rule applies on every harness; (b) 'I do not know yet' becomes a committed `open` decision row with an owner and a revisit gate (extending the existing `__defer` escape), not a route back to private chat; (c) panels, diagrams and prototypes are opted into per risk tier by a per-project policy line the team commits in AGENTS.md, so five developers run the same ceremony for the same tier, and prototypes are throwaway with a reconciliation step to the spec like design Step 3, or are not shipped; (d) the decision-dossier pilot's kill criterion is adjudicated on the record first (count bypasses since 2026-07-20) and one team feature's panel is priced in tokens and hours before 'standard' is written anywhere.

On the human's position

The maintainer's words: "the artifacts are not the problem — answering questions directly inside them is 'amazing' once the idea is clear. The failure is timing… the switch should key on clarity, not on which skill is running," plus "'I don't know yet / explore this' as a first-class answer in every artifact question that routes back to chat or to a panel," and Q2: "if I can get it to work best for me, we can easily get it for others." Three attacks from this lens. First, "amazing" is the Claude super-user's experience with the db-published page; the colleague on Codex gets a localStorage page and a paste-back block (interactive-checkpoint.md:46-50), so "once the idea is clear" describes one harness's surface, not the team's. Second, "key on clarity" names the right variable and then leaves it to the agent or to whoever is at the keyboard; on a team the person who is unclear is often not the person answering (team-ready-gates: a PM collects answers from other teams), so the signal must be a declared, committed state, not an inference. Third, "routes back to chat" is the wrong destination for a team: chat is the one place no second developer can read. The repo already solved this once with defer-to-person (D2/D11), which turns an unknown into an owner and a visible line. Q2's "works for me, then for others" is the exact transfer this lens denies: the super-user's clarity threshold, prototype discipline and panel habit are personal, and the tally shows even the super-user applied the bookend to 6 of 13 features. My lens moves the position, not to rejection but to a condition: keep the clarity switch as a human-declared 'still exploring / ready to decide' state; make 'I do not know yet' a recorded `open` row with an owner and a revisit gate, never a route to chat; and make panels and prototypes a per-project tier policy the team commits in AGENTS.md, so all five engineers pay the same ceremony for the same risk tier.

Maintainer counting hoursqualified
Strongest refutation

P9 as written buys three new product surfaces (a panel step, new visual artifact types, a clarity detector plus a fifth answer state) for a problem the repo's own record says to solve by subtraction, and it does so on the surface that already eats most of the maintainer's hours. (1) The kill criterion already fired. The Deposition Checkpoint shipped with "kill the format if Max bypasses the questions into free chat by the second feature" (docs/features/2026-07-20-decision-dossier/brief.md:89-91; RF mechanism 4 at docs/features/2026-07-20-reading-fatigue-panel/research.md:47-49). No decision-log row ever records the pilot surviving (grep of docs/context/decision-log.md for dossier/pilot/kill returns none), the format propagated to user-facing skills anyway, and the evidence pack's own header records the bypass: "Origin: /joycraft-interview session (chat-only, no gate artifacts by request)" (docs/research/2026-09-24-dynamic-joycraft-evidence.md:5). P9's "I do not know yet routes back to chat" legitimizes the exact behavior the pilot named as its kill signal, without saying which of the two was wrong. (2) The design bookend is already where the hours go. Five of the ten releases from 0.7.0 to 0.7.11 (2026-07-21 to 2026-09-03, six weeks) were gate/artifact/output-style work (CHANGELOG.md:179-439); since 2026-07-01 there are 49 commits touching src/skills, 18 touching src/templates, 102 touching tests; gate machinery alone carries 1,686 test lines (tests/gate-contract.test.ts 830, interactive-checkpoint 254, review-gate-template 215, gate-slot-contract-placement 210, artifact-render-steps 177), and the gate-contract test pins exact skill counts ("covers exactly the five question-bearing skills", tests/gate-contract.test.ts:209; PRE_PRESENTATION_SKILLS :93-99), so every new gate skill or answer state edits at least five exact-count assertions, the checkpoint template (487 lines), the protocol doc, five harness trees via sync-skills, and a CHANGELOG line for the docs-sync gate. (3) Panels have no product mechanism at all (grep 'panel' in src/skills/*.md: zero hits) and the repo's panels ran at 3, 13, 52 and "roughly fifty Opus 5.5 agents" (docs/backlog/2026-09-23-checkpoint-non-claude-harnesses.md:9; decision-log.md:36; reading-fatigue research.md:5; docs/research/2026-09-24-dynamic-joycraft-checkpoint.html:365). Making that a "standard step" per feature is a token bill nobody has measured, and the risk-tiering that would cap it has a precedent that says it cannot be automatic: decision-log 2026-05-30 kept the size-to-mode heuristic human-approved because "only a human knows" risk (decision-log.md:94). A human-decided, hand-run panel is what exists today for free. (4) Visuals: succinct-gates D1 deliberately chose one generic REVIEW_GATE template because "per-gate templates multiply the render-check surface for no structural gain" (decision-log.md:70); sequence/data-flow/mockup/prototype templates reverse that decision, and prototypes would be files outside every manifest kind (src/install-manifest.ts:30 has only vendor | create-once | config-patch), never cleaned, on a repo where the folder map is already never regenerated after first install (evidence pack 8.4). (5) The checkpoint P9 wants to gate on clarity only works on Claude; every other harness gets paste-back (backlog 2026-09-23-checkpoint-non-claude-harnesses.md:11), which is RF-KILL-6 "do not rebuild" (reading-fatigue research.md:62-63). The server that fixes it is itself deferred as "its own feature" (same backlog:17).

Qualification

P9 stands only in its subtractive form, on existing surfaces, with nothing new to sync or test: (a) one sentence added to the shared question-directive paragraph in the eight gate skills — while the human says they are still exploring, stay in chat and render no checkpoint; the human, not the agent, signals clarity; (b) one added escape key in the existing CHECKPOINT_TEMPLATE.html and interactive-checkpoint.md (an 'explore' escape that leaves the question open and returns to chat), which is a fifth terminal state and therefore touches decide.md, the five PRE_PRESENTATION skills, and the gate-contract tests once; (c) the dossier pilot's bypass-to-chat criterion is re-read as 'bypass while unclear is expected; bypass once clear kills the format' and is stamped in the decision log so the contradiction closes. Not in scope: a panel skill or panel step (panels stay hand-run and human-decided per feature, as today, until a token cost per panel is measured on at least two features); new diagram, mockup, or prototype templates (the agent may draw an inline SVG inside the existing design.html or review-gate render when it helps, under D1's one-template rule); any agent-side clarity detector; any 'risk tier' automation beyond the human-approved mode heuristic that already exists. Condition for revisiting the excluded pieces: the non-Claude checkpoint server ships first (otherwise every added ceremony lands on four harnesses as RF-KILL-6 paste-back), and one measured panel cost exists.

On the human's position

The maintainer's own words in section 10 and the P9 clarification cut both ways. Q1: 'the formality of the loop, getting people used to TDD agentic development as opposed to endless vibe coding' — P9 pushes formality earlier into brainstorming, which is exactly where his clarification says formality 'becomes a hindrance'. Q2: 'if I can get it to work best for me, we can easily get it for others' — the maintainer is the one user who runs ~50-agent panels by hand and reads HTML dossiers for fun; a step tuned to him is the worst predictor of what fifteen colleagues on Codex and Pi (paste-back checkpoints, RF-KILL-6) will tolerate. Q4: 'in recent sessions I've been getting some slop that took hours and that was not shippable, we have to close that gap' — this is the honest motive for P9, but it is evidence for blocking gates in the implement loop (P3), not for more design-bookend ceremony; the pack's Helix citation, checked live, puts its one human pre-step at approving a checkpoint list 'in minutes'. Q8: 'no brief though, as you and I will have follow up discussion' — he chose chat over artifacts again for the highest-stakes decision in the repo's history, which is the dossier kill criterion firing a third time. His clarification that 'the artifacts are not the problem ... the failure is timing' and 'the switch should key on clarity, not on which skill is running' is correct and cheap: it is one sentence in the existing directive plus one escape key. My lens moves his position only on the additions: the panel-as-standard-step and the diagram/prototype templates are new surfaces on the part of the product that already consumed five of the last ten releases and 1,686 test lines, and his own decision log (2026-05-30, 'only a human knows' risk; 2026-07-29 D1, one template not N) says to keep both as human-decided, hand-run practice rather than shipped mechanism until a cost is measured.

Evidence auditorqualified
Strongest refutation

P9 has no external evidence behind it, and its one external anchor is misread. The lead cites Helix ("moves feedback to the earliest useful point") for front-loading design; the live article (shopify.engineering/helix, 2026-09-21) has no design, spec, diagram, prototype or panel phase before code — the engineer only approves a checkpoint *sequence*, then reviews "the code and running app" per small checkpoint, and "the reference is the spec." Helix front-loads verification of working code, not design artifacts; it is evidence against P9's shape, not for it. Every other P9 support is internal and self-reported: "panel" appears in zero of the 22 skills, "prototype"/"mockup" in none, "diagram" once (decide.md:135, optional); the checkpoint artifact the maintainer calls "amazing" has exactly one committed render on this branch (docs/features/2026-09-22-fable-native-sdlc-harness/checkpoint-decide.html) plus two on the parked branch, all from 2026-09-22..24 — roughly two days of use, n=1, no metric, and docs/.joycraft/telemetry.json records zero checkpoint, design.md, panel, or cost events. The repo also holds a direct counterexample: the Opus 5.5 feature went through the full front-loaded ceremony — checkpoint-new-feature.html (D1–D8), brief approved (D9, 2026-09-24), checkpoint-decompose.html, 9 specs totaling 871 lines — and was parked the same day (evidence pack header). Front-loading did not stop spec tokens landing on what the human then did not want. And the maintainer's own 52-agent reading-fatigue brief (2026-07-20) names the pre-spec design doc as the failure mode ("The rubber-stamped design review... a fluent 200-line design doc... you read fifteen lines, think 'looks right,' and approve"), prescribes "delete nominal output, tier the channels... demand decisions instead of reading," and set the Deposition Checkpoint a 4-week pilot with "kill if you bypass to chat" — a criterion never instrumented (no bypass tracking in src/ or telemetry) before the checkpoint shipped in 0.7.1, and which the maintainer's own P9 clarification ("in full brainstorm mode... becomes a hindrance") reports triggering. Adding panels and prototypes as standard steps on top of a design gate already skipped in 50 of 60 feature folders (10 have design.md; 13 of the 23 spec'd features skipped design entirely) is asking for more of the ceremony the evidence says gets skipped or rubber-stamped.

Qualification

P9 stands only as: (1) a readiness switch plus a first-class "I do not know yet / explore this" escape added to the existing checkpoint protocol (edits to src/skills/joycraft-interview.md:39,44, src/skills/joycraft-new-feature.md:61-68, docs/templates/reference/interactive-checkpoint.md:9,31), which needs no new artifact type; and (2) risk-tiered diagrams inside the existing design gate. Panels and prototypes as standard per-feature steps are not supported by any citation and must ship as a pilot with the instrumentation the July 2026 brief already demanded: bypass-to-chat and skip rate tracked in telemetry, a per-panel token cost recorded, and a before/after on rework or parked-after-approval features. Drop Helix as a citation for front-loading design; it supports gating implemented checkpoints (Q4), not pre-spec artifacts.
