On the human's position

The maintainer's words (§9 clarification): "the artifacts are not the problem — answering questions directly inside them is 'amazing' once the idea is clear. The failure is timing"; and (§0) hand-run panels and prototypes drive "quality up far more than discovering after the implement-feature loop that 'it's all garbage.'" Audited: "amazing" rests on three checkpoint renders dated 2026-09-22..24 — about two days of one user's use, no metric, and no telemetry — and the brainstorm-mode "hindrance" is literally the Deposition Checkpoint's July kill signal ("bypass to chat") reframed as a timing bug after the pilot graduated without its criterion ever being tracked. The "it's all garbage" comparison has no control: the slop sessions in Q4 ("some slop that took hours and that was not shippable") happened with design, decide and the checkpoint already shipped, so the existing front-loaded gates did not prevent the failure the maintainer wants fixed — that points at the implementation gate (Q4, Helix's actual mechanism), not at more design ceremony. And the one fully front-loaded feature in the repo (Opus 5.5: two checkpoints, approved brief, 9 specs) was parked the day it was approved. My lens moves the position in two directions. It strengthens the narrow part: the ≥2-questions rule at interview.md:39,44 and the missing 'I do not know yet' escape at interactive-checkpoint.md:31 are real, cheap defects, and Fable 5's own guide ('Pause for the user only when the work genuinely requires them') supports switching on need rather than on skill boundary. It weakens the broad part: panels and prototypes as standard steps have zero supporting citations, Helix cannot be cited for them, and the maintainer's own 52-agent verdict predicts they will be skipped (50 of 60 features skipped the design gate) or rubber-stamped. Argue 'switch on clarity' as a fix and 'panels as standard' as an experiment with the kill criterion the July brief already wrote.

P10 · 4 skeptics

Architecture-defense session as setup step and maturity gate

qualify
Ruling

P10 is qualified. The practice survives (agent surfaces the architecture, human corrects, corrections are recorded), but the phrase "enforceable architecture record" does not: nothing in Joycraft can enforce or re-check a prose architecture record, and the claim's own cited precedent (Helix) runs in the opposite direction, with a human-designed architecture enforced by reviewers checking code. It stands only when each correction terminates as a machine check or a decision-log row that an independent verifier reads and re-derives, it is an opt-in maturity mode of the design bookend rather than a universal setup step, and it ships as a measured pilot.

The claim as argued

At setup and as the project matures, the agent proposes the architecture, defends it with code examples, explains each decision; the human corrects; the corrections become the enforceable architecture record (Helix: documented architecture makes adversarial review enforceable; the reading-fatigue "theory ledger"). Skeptic angles: the human is the only verifier of the corrections, so what re-checks them as code drifts; the context map is "hopeful disclosure" so does the record get read; cost on a mature codebase; duplication with design, decide, and dangerous-assumptions; teams where corrector and implementer differ.

Replacement claim

Not a flip; the qualified claim reads: an architecture-confirmation session, run as an opt-in mode of the design bookend on existing code, in which the agent extracts the architecture from code with file:line evidence and the human corrects it; each correction lands in the same commit as a machine check or an owner-stamped decision-log row that joycraft-verify reads as oracle input and re-derives on drift triggers; piloted with a measured delta before it becomes a default gate.

Condition

P10 holds only under all of the following: (1) FORM: every human correction terminates, in the same commit, as exactly one of (a) a machine check the project owns (a harden deny pattern where the rule is path/regex-shaped per src/skills/joycraft-harden.md:33-37, otherwise a CI dependency/lint/test check such as a dependency-cruiser rule) or (b) a decision-log row (Date, Decision, Why, Alternatives, Revisit When, plus owner) in docs/context/decision-log.md; a correction that fits neither is discarded, not recorded; no new standalone architecture document and no Context Map pointer is created. (2) READER: src/skills/joycraft-verify.md Step 2.5 is extended so the verifier's oracle includes those decision-log rows, and a fresh-context subagent re-derives the recorded architecture against code when an evidence trigger fires (a verify FINDING, folder-map drift reported by tune, or a NEVER_READ telemetry verdict), so the human is not the only verifier. (3) PLACEMENT: it is not a step on the universal setup path. Greenfield reduces to joycraft-design Sections 3 and 4, which already exist. On existing code it is an explicit opt-in project-scope mode of design/decide that extracts rules from code for the human to confirm (Helix's direction), with the token cost stated up front, honoring src/skills/joycraft-gather-context.md:27. (4) TEAMS: one named owner per repo runs the session and commits the record; other engineers' sessions read it as a constraint and file corrections through the same owner-stamped path, never re-proposing the architecture. (5) EVIDENCE: it ships as a pilot with a pre-committed before/after count (verify FINDINGS per feature, or the maintainer's own hours-of-unshippable-output) because the only supporting evidence today is one uncontrolled self-report.

Judge's reasoning

All four skeptics returned "qualified"; none argued the practice is worthless and none argued the claim stands as written, and the evidence supports that split. Against "keep": the word "enforceable" has no mechanism. harden.md:19-20 names permissions.deny and deny-patterns.txt as "the only two enforcement surfaces" and :33-40 classes semantic rules ("repositories go through the service layer") as ineligible prose; verify.md Step 2.5's oracle is brief Hard Constraints + decisions frontmatter + boundary file and never reads the decision log or any architecture doc; implement reads nothing under docs/context (grep empty); design's retrieval is a grep capped at 5 rows (design.md:19-27). So after the human corrects once, no reader on the implement path and no re-check exists, which is the proposition's own first skeptic angle, confirmed in the repo. The Helix citation, which I fetched, holds verbatim but is misapplied: the architecture was designed by humans ("a highly opinionated architecture we designed"), the document is a standard "so reviewers have a standard to enforce", enforcement is two context-isolated reviewer agents over code, and the page is silent on memory storage and on re-verifying documentation against code. P10 inverts the direction (agent proposes) and borrows the word "enforceable" without the reviewers. The repo also shows the drift failure in miniature: the folder map, a machine-derivable record, is regenerated only on create-once generation paths (agents-md.ts:148, improve-claude-md.ts:414) and AGENTS.md has no docs/intent row while the folder exists; a hand-corrected prose record would drift faster. The setup-step framing collides with gather-context.md:27's explicit no-code-scan cost rule and with the pack's own constraint that the practice "requires a CS background". Against "flip": the decision log survived a six-panelist trial 6/6 with an in-repo demonstration of reuse; Helix explicitly records reviewer feedback so autonomy grows; Anthropic's Fable guidance recommends recording corrections and fresh-context verifiers; the ETH study finds instructions in context files are followed even though success does not rise, so the failure mode is reads and drift, not compliance; and the escalation rule in add-fact.md:24 and session-end.md:64 already routes enforceable facts to harden, giving P10's outputs a legitimate home. The practice therefore has value under conditions the skeptics converge on: check-or-row form, a verifier reader, opt-in on existing code, one owner on teams, and a pilot. The five conditions above are the union of their qualifications where they agree and my resolution where they split (see skeptic_disagreements).

Strongest refutation considered

The harness-expert's combined argument: P10 produces the one artifact class the repo has already ruled unenforceable (harden.md:13 "Prose is a rule the model merely hopes to follow"), Joycraft has no mechanism to re-check it, and the repo's own check-shaped record (the folder map) decayed within weeks, so a human-corrected prose record with no re-deriver will drift faster while, per Ronacher, appearing more robust; joined to the team-lead's point that Helix runs the opposite direction (human-designed reference, reviewers enforce over code). I weighed this as nearly a flip. It does not flip because the refutation attacks the recording form and the missing reader, both of which are fixable and named by every skeptic, and not the practice's core: a memory of human corrections is load-bearing in Helix ("Helix records it in memory to improve every checkpoint that follows"), is a vendor-recommended pattern (record corrections; fresh-context verifiers), and the decision log already demonstrates in-repo that recorded rationale is reused. So the honest outcome is a narrowed claim, not a reversal.

Human position moved?

Yes, on three points, with evidence. (1) Q4 'gates that cannot be overridden' and 'we have to close that gap' on unshippable output: the panel showed P10 as written is not a gate. verify.md Step 2.5 never reads an architecture record, harden.md:33-40 cannot convert one, and implement reads nothing under docs/context, so a setup-time document cannot close a gap on a path that never opens it. The Helix mechanism the maintainer admires is verifier-side (reviewers checking code against a human-designed standard), not a defense ceremony. The position moves from 'record the corrections' to 'the corrections become checks or verifier-oracle rows'. (2) Q1 'gates + lifecycle + artifacts fixed; process prose generated': by the maintainer's own rule the architecture record is generated prose and therefore not part of the invariant; only the check or verifier input derived from it is. The §0 phrasing 'corrections become a core part of the context map' is the weakest possible form and is rejected by every skeptic on the context-map panel's 'hopeful disclosure' finding (verdict line 57). (3) Q2 'one path' versus the §0 constraint 'requires a CS background': the team-lead is right that both cannot hold for a mandatory setup step. The panel does not force a P11-style fork; it resolves it as an opt-in mode of the existing design bookend on existing code, which keeps one path. Not moved: the maintainer's belief that the practice itself reduces slop-on-slop. The skeptics could not refute it, only note it is one uncontrolled report confounded by the practitioner's skill, hence the pilot condition.

Skeptic disagreements

  • Where the record lives. harness-expert: a project-scope mode of design/decide writing to the decision log, no new skill or doc. team-lead: fold into joycraft-design's per-feature review gate. ai-researcher: a distinct maturity gate on existing code only. evidence-auditor: primarily a verifier oracle, form secondary. Resolved in condition (1)-(3): decision-log rows + checks, as an opt-in mode of the design bookend.
  • Whether architecture rules can become checks in Joycraft today. evidence-auditor: no, harden's two surfaces cannot express architecture rules (harden.md:35-37), so 'enforceable' is limited to what a verifier can check. harness-expert and ai-researcher: yes via CI dependency rules (dependency-cruiser), which are outside harden's surfaces. Both are correct on their own terms; condition (1a) admits project-owned CI checks, not only harden.
  • Whether a short directive record could go in the always-loaded file. team-lead reads the ETH 'instructions are well followed' finding as support for an L1 placement of a short directive record. harness-expert, ai-researcher and evidence-auditor keep it out of L1 and out of the Context Map (context-map panel: L1 is directional content only). I side with the majority: L1 is not a home for architecture rules; that is the accretion Ronacher and the ThoughtWorks bloat paper describe.
  • Pilot as a precondition. Only the ai-researcher requires a measured before/after delta before shipping; the other three accept the practice with structural conditions alone. I adopt the pilot (condition 5) because the sole positive evidence is an n=1 self-report and the maintainer's Q4 complaint is countable.
  • Owner column on teams. team-lead requires one named owner and an owner column on rows; ai-researcher notes collaborative-setup records area owners but nothing ties a correction to an owner; harness-expert and evidence-auditor do not address ownership. Adopted as condition (4).
  • Trigger for the maturity re-run. harness-expert: evidence triggers only (drift diff, NEVER_READ, verifier failure), never calendar. ai-researcher: 'a fixed cadence'. evidence-auditor: 'on a schedule'. I side with evidence triggers; a calendar re-run on a mature codebase is unpriced cost with no signal.
  • Folder-map regeneration. harness-expert (and evidence pack §8.4) say ensureFolderMapSection 'is called only by tests'; ai-researcher correctly says it is reached from the generation paths (src/agents-md.ts:148, src/improve-claude-md.ts:414) and only diffFolderMap is tests-only. Same conclusion (never regenerated after creation), different fact.
  • Cost of the setup instance. ai-researcher: greenfield has no code to defend, so setup reduces to design Sections 3-4. team-lead and harness-expert: the setup instance is a cost reversal of gather-context.md:27. evidence-auditor: practitioner-tier maturity gate at most. All reject a universal setup step; they differ on whether a greenfield instance is redundant or merely costly.
  • Reading of the maintainer's Q2 'one path'. team-lead: Q2 and the CS-background constraint cannot both hold, so the maintainer must pick a fork (P11) or make it optional. harness-expert: fine for the maintainer-first path, breaks when corrector and implementer differ. I rule that an opt-in mode preserves one path better than a background fork.

Citation problems

  • Evidence pack §8.4 and the harness-expert state that ensureFolderMapSection 'is now called only by tests'. False: it is called from src/agents-md.ts:148 and src/improve-claude-md.ts:414 (the create-once generation paths). Only diffFolderMap is tests-only. The conclusion that the folder map is never regenerated after first creation survives; the literal claim does not.
  • Evidence pack P10 and §0 apply Helix's 'This documentation makes adversarial review enforceable' to a human-corrected record produced by an agent-proposed architecture. The live page (fetched by the judge) says the architecture was designed by humans, the documentation is a standard for reviewers, and enforcement is two reviewer agents checking code. The quote holds; the transfer is not in the source.
  • Evidence pack P10 says the Theory Ledger was 'called "the strongest single idea"'. The reading-fatigue brief (docs/research/2026-07-20-reading-fatigue-brief.html:370) says 'arguably the strongest single idea'; the research.md:42 summary drops the hedge. Minor, flagged by the evidence-auditor.
  • Evidence pack §4.1 SkillsBench figures are from a stale version per the ai-researcher's live fetch of v4 (2026-06-14): +16.6pp over 87 tasks, self-generated skills below baseline (-8.1 to -11.5pp) rather than 'no benefit', Software Engineering +11.6pp rather than +4.5pp, 13 of 87 tasks negative. Not P10-central; direction survives.
  • The context-map panel verdict (2026-09-01, line 54) cites the ETH context-file study as arXiv 2601.20404 with a '+4% hand-written' figure; the evidence pack cites 2602.11988. No skeptic reconciled the two ids or checked the +4% figure.
  • Ronacher's accretion quote (lucumr.pocoo.org 2026-06-23, evidence pack §1.8) was not re-fetched by any skeptic; relied on the pack's transcription.
  • DCBench (arXiv 2605.08112) '+49% decision-compliance' as used by the context-map panel omits, per the ai-researcher's fetch, that the gain was confined to decisions invisible in source code and that the benchmark was authored by the vendor of the product under test; architecture decisions are mostly visible in code, so this figure supports P10 less than the lineage suggests.

What would change the ruling

Toward keep (claim stands with a plain human-read record): a with/without run on this repo or a colleague's project showing that a prose architecture record, read only by humans and not fed to verify, measurably reduces verify FINDINGS or the maintainer's hours of unshippable output; or telemetry showing the decision log is voluntarily read in more than 20% of feature-shaped sessions, which would weaken the 'no reader' objection. Toward flip (drop the practice): a pilot under conditions (1)-(2) in which the record is fed to verify and re-derived on drift and FINDINGS still do not fall; an ETH-style measurement on this repo showing the record adds cost with no delta; or an ACE-style collapse of the record's content after several maturity re-runs. Also load-bearing: any published account of how Helix stores feedback memory (prose vs checks vs examples) would settle whether the precedent supports a document at all.

Skeptics

Agent-harness expertqualified
Strongest refutation

P10 as filed produces the one artifact class this repo has already ruled unenforceable: prose the model is hoped to read. Helix's "documentation makes adversarial review enforceable" holds on the live page, but the enforcement there is two context-isolated blocking reviewers plus "the reference *is* the spec" (code, not a document); the page says nothing about re-verifying recorded corrections as code changes (ABSENT). Joycraft has no mechanism to re-check an architecture record either: `harden` converts only command-regex/file-path rules and labels every semantic rule ineligible (src/skills/joycraft-harden.md:33-40, and :13 says "Prose is a rule the model merely hopes to follow"); the four shipped hook recipes are path guards and a non-blocking plan reminder (docs/templates/hooks/README.md:23-26); `verify`'s oracle is spec + brief + boundaries, never an architecture doc (src/skills/joycraft-verify.md, Step 2.5). Worse, the repo's own "check-shaped" architecture record already decayed: the folder map is create-once and `ensureFolderMapSection` is called only by tests (src/update-inventory.ts:225-262; evidence pack §8.4), and AGENTS.md has no `docs/intent` row although the folder exists (grep on AGENTS.md returns nothing). A generated, machine-derivable map drifted in three weeks; a human-corrected prose record with no re-deriver will drift faster and, per Ronacher, "each iteration adds another small defense… less understandable while appearing more robust" (evidence §1.8). Finally it duplicates `design`, which already spawns codebase subagents, cites `file:line` snippets, records Resolved Design Decisions and option-bearing Open Questions (src/skills/joycraft-design.md:40-107), and it reverses `gather-context`'s explicit setup-time decision not to run a code-inference scan for cost (src/skills/joycraft-gather-context.md:27).

Qualification

P10 survives only under all of: (1) every human correction terminates in one of exactly two forms in the same commit — a machine check (dependency-cruiser/ArchUnit-style dependency rule, lint rule, protected-path hook, or test) or an entry in a capped ledger (≤600 words, the reading-fatigue Theory Ledger's shape) that a fresh-context verifier re-derives at the PR bookend; a correction that fits neither is discarded, not recorded; (2) it runs as a project-scope mode of `design`/`decide` writing to the decision log (the one context doc all six panelists kept), not a new skill or a new doc; (3) on a mature codebase the agent extracts rules from existing code and the human confirms (Helix's "reference is the spec"), rather than proposing-and-defending from scratch; (4) the maturity re-run is triggered by evidence (drift diff, telemetry NEVER_READ, verifier failure), not by calendar. Without (1) it is advice, and the maintainer's own Q4 asks for gates that cannot be overridden.

On the human's position

The maintainer filed no P10-specific checkpoint answer; the position comes from §0 (colleague's practice, "much less slop, especially the 'slop on slop' that accretes as a project matures"; "requires a CS background") and bears on Q1 and Q4. Q1: "Gates + lifecycle + artifacts fixed; process prose generated." P10 as written generates prose and then treats it as a gate — that is the exact category confusion Q1 rules out. Q4: "Gates that cannot be overridden… in recent sessions I've been getting some slop that took hours and that was not shippable, we have to close that gap." An architecture record nobody re-checks cannot close a shippability gap; it can only describe what should have happened. The maintainer's own harness says so: harden.md:13 ("Prose is a rule the model merely hopes to follow") and session-end.md:64 routes any fact "enforceable as architecture, a deny pattern, or a CI check" to harden, not prose. So my lens moves the position in one direction: keep the session, but change what a correction is allowed to become — a check in the same commit, or a capped ledger entry that a fresh-context verifier re-derives; otherwise discard it. On "requires a CS background": for the maintainer-first path (Q2) this is fine, but the moment corrector and implementer differ across the fifteen colleagues, only the check form binds the implementer; the prose form binds nobody who did not attend the session. The "defend with code examples" ritual is the cheap, visible part and the least valuable: on a mature codebase the code already is the defense (Helix: "the reference is the spec"); let the agent extract rules from it and have the human confirm.

Team lead, five engineersqualified
Strongest refutation

"Enforceable architecture record" is a category error in Joycraft as wired. The only enforcement surfaces are deny-patterns.txt and permissions.deny (src/skills/joycraft-harden.md:19-20), and harden explicitly classes semantic/judgment rules as ineligible and leaves them as prose (harden.md:33-40). An architecture correction ("no, repositories go through the service layer") is exactly that class. The one independent verifier Joycraft has reads spec + brief hard constraints + decisions frontmatter + boundaries (src/skills/joycraft-verify.md:34-42); it never reads an architecture record or the decision log. So after the human corrects, nothing re-checks the correction as code drifts — the proposition's own skeptic angle is confirmed by the repo. On a five-person team that is fatal: five engineers each get a different agent-proposed architecture, correct it differently (juniors cannot correct at all — the pack's own constraint, evidence §0 line 23: "requires a CS background"), the record has no owner column (src/templates/context/decision-log.md: Date | Decision | Why | Alternatives | Revisit When), and the reviewer now carries two review loads — the diff and whether the diff honored an un-machine-checked document. Helix, the cited precedent, runs the opposite direction: a human-designed, fixed reference architecture that agents implement, enforced by two context-isolated reviewer agents, not by the document (shopify.engineering/helix, checked 2026-09-24). And Joycraft already has this step per feature: design spawns subagents to read code (joycraft-design.md:42), shows patterns as code snippets with file:line (93-95), states resolved decisions with rationale (99-104), the human corrects at a blocking review gate (277, 303-304), and decide stamps the result into the decision log (joycraft-decide.md:253). A setup-time repeat that reads the whole codebase reverses gather-context's deliberate cost decision (joycraft-gather-context.md:27: "Do NOT auto-run a code-inference scan") with no new evidence.

Qualification

P10 stands for a team only under all four conditions: (1) every correction terminates as a machine check (harden deny pattern, CI assertion, or lint) or as a decision-log row with an explicit owner and 'Revisit when' — never as free prose in the context map or AGENTS.md; (2) that record becomes an oracle input to joycraft-verify Step 2.5 so a fresh-context verifier re-derives it against the code at every PR bookend (the Theory Ledger's 'independent verifier re-derives periodically'), and drift fails the gate instead of waiting for a human to notice; (3) on a team, exactly one named owner runs the defense session and commits the record; the other engineers' sessions read it as a constraint and may only file corrections through the same owner-stamped path, never re-propose the architecture; (4) it is a per-feature step at the design bookend for practitioners (folded into joycraft-design, which already does 80% of it), not a mandatory setup step on the 'one path' — gated on P11's background flag or on the owner opting in. Without (1) and (2) it is refuted: a document the human alone verifies is exactly the 'hopeful disclosure' the last panel condemned. Without (3) it produces five divergent architecture records for one codebase.

On the human's position

The maintainer's Q4 answer is 'Gates that cannot be overridden' and the gap to close is 'full confidence of when that loop is done they have shippable product.' P10 as written is not a gate: it is a document produced at setup that the human corrects once and that nothing re-checks (verify.md:34-42 never reads it; harden.md:33-40 cannot convert it). So on the maintainer's own Q4 standard, P10 as a 'maturity gate' is mislabeled — it is advice with a ceremony. My lens moves it: the human should demand that each correction land as a check or an owner-stamped decision row, or drop the word 'enforceable'. Q2 says 'one path' for 'about 15 colleagues... across different size teams... mixed skill', and the pack's own §0 says the architecture-defense practice 'requires a CS background, so it is useless for Joycraft's novice users.' Those two positions cannot both hold for P10: either the defense session is optional (then it is not a setup step or a gate on the one path) or the path forks by background (which is P11 and contradicts 'one path'). The maintainer must pick; my lens says make it the practitioner-only form of the existing design review gate, owned by one person per repo, and keep novices on the corrected record as a read-only constraint. Q1 ('gates + lifecycle + artifacts fixed; process prose generated') actually supports my qualification: the architecture record is generated prose and therefore by the maintainer's own rule is not part of the invariant — only the check derived from it is.

AI researcherqualified
Strongest refutation

P10 rests on zero measured deltas and on an analogy that does not transfer. The only direct evidence is one colleague's self-report ("He reports much less slop", evidence pack §0, docs/research/2026-09-24-dynamic-joycraft-evidence.md:22), n=1, no baseline, not on Joycraft. The Helix quote holds verbatim (shopify.engineering/helix, 2026-09-21), but in Helix the documentation is an upfront engineer-written reference for a fixed target architecture, and enforcement comes from two context-isolated reviewer agents plus blocking gates, not from the document; the article says nothing about how memory is stored or how docs stay in sync with code (confirmed absent on live fetch). The closest measured analog to "an architecture record in the repo's context files" is the ETH study (arXiv 2602.11988, 2026-02-12, rev 2026-06-23): repository context files, developer-written or LLM-generated, "do not generally improve task success rates, while increasing inference cost by over 20% on average". The one positive result, DCBench (arXiv 2605.08112, 2026-04-27, +49pp decision compliance, 46%→95%), explicitly found the baseline already at full compliance on decisions visible in the source code; the gain lived entirely on decisions invisible in code (product/persona/customer context). Architecture decisions are mostly visible in code, so DCBench's gain lands where P10 contributes least. In-repo, the record has no reader on the path where the maintainer says the slop occurs: joycraft-verify's oracle is brief Hard Constraints + brief decisions frontmatter + boundary file (src/skills/joycraft-verify.md:34-42, 100) and never docs/context/decision-log.md; joycraft-implement reads no docs/context file at all (grep empty); design reads the decision log via a grep capped at 5 rows (src/skills/joycraft-design.md:17-30). The repo already demonstrates the drift failure P10 would repeat: tune.md:63 says upgrade regenerates the folder map, but ensureFolderMapSection is reached only from the generation paths (src/agents-md.ts:148, src/improve-claude-md.ts:414) and diffFolderMap only from tests/folder-map.test.ts:111-127, while AGENTS.md is create-once (src/update-inventory.ts:236-262) — so the one check-shaped architecture artifact Joycraft ships is never re-checked. A prose architecture record would be worse: no check at all.

Qualification

P10 stands only under all three conditions: (1) every correction from the session terminates as a machine check (dependency rule, deny pattern, CI assertion, via harden) or as a decision-log row, never as a standalone prose architecture record; (2) joycraft-verify's oracle (verify.md:34-42) is extended to read those rows, and a fresh-context re-derivation of the record against code runs at a fixed cadence, so a reader exists on the implement path; (3) it ships as a maturity gate on existing code, not a greenfield setup step, and only after a pilot measures a delta (verify FINDINGS rate, or a DCBench-style compliance probe on the project's own corrections) against sessions without it. Absent (1)-(2) the record is hopeful disclosure that the ETH null result says costs >20% for nothing; absent (3) the sole evidence remains one uncontrolled self-report.

Evidence for the refutation

  • Repository context files, hand-written or generated, do not improve task success and add >20% inference cost; instructions in them are followed. So a prose architecture record buys compliance with what it says, not better outcomes, at a cost. arXiv 2602.11988 abstract, live fetch 2026-09-24 (submitted 2026-02-12, revised 2026-06-23)
  • The +49pp decision-compliance gain came from decisions invisible in the source (baseline 0-33% there) while the baseline was already fully compliant on decisions visible in code; 8 tasks, 41 decision points, benchmark authored by the vendor of the product under test (Brief), context delivered by retrieval at spec time and mid-build, not by a human-corrected document. arXiv 2605.08112 abstract, live fetch 2026-09-24 (submitted 2026-04-27)
  • Agent-authored knowledge artifacts land below the no-artifact baseline (-8.1 to -11.5pp) and the audit attributes it to packs the solver never discovers, authoring that displaces solving work, and confidently wrong content. P10's proposal step is agent-authored; only the human correction distinguishes it, and 'never discovers' is exactly the hopeful-disclosure read problem. arXiv 2602.12670v4 (2026-06-14), live fetch 2026-09-24, section 'Self-generated Skills do not substitute for curated ones'
  • Iterative rewriting of a knowledge context erodes detail (context collapse); a record appended and rewritten at every maturity gate is that pattern unless updates are structured and curated. arXiv 2510.04618 abstract, live fetch 2026-09-24 (submitted 2025-10-06, rev 2026-03-29)
  • Helix's documentation is an upfront reference for a fixed target architecture; enforcement is two context-isolated adversarial reviewers plus gates the agent cannot override. The article does not describe how feedback memory is stored or how documentation tracks code. https://shopify.engineering/helix, Talha Naqvi, 2026-09-21, live fetch 2026-09-24
  • verify's oracle is brief Hard Constraints + decisions frontmatter + boundary file; the decision log and any architecture doc are not oracle inputs. implement reads nothing under docs/context. src/skills/joycraft-verify.md:34-42, 90-108; grep of src/skills/joycraft-implement.md for docs/context returns nothing
  • design's retrieval of prior decisions is a grep capped at 5 files/rows; a growing corrections record is read only where its terms happen to match. src/skills/joycraft-design.md:17-30
  • The existing check-shaped architecture artifact is not re-checked: tune says upgrade regenerates the folder map, but regeneration is only reachable from the generation paths and drift-diff is only called by tests; AGENTS.md is create-once. src/skills/joycraft-tune.md:58-63; src/agents-md.ts:148; src/improve-claude-md.ts:414; tests/folder-map.test.ts:111-127; src/update-inventory.ts:236-262
  • Joycraft's own onboarding refuses to read source to infer architecture by default because it 'costs significantly more tokens'. A code-example-backed defense on a mature codebase is that scan, and no cost has been measured. src/skills/joycraft-gather-context.md:27
  • Prior Joycraft panels already ruled that must-read content is disqualified from the pointer tier, that the Context Map is 'hopeful disclosure, not progressive disclosure', and that a doc with zero voluntary reads after 30 sessions/60 days is a RETIRE candidate. No telemetry run has yet shown the decision log is read voluntarily. docs/research/2026-09-01-context-map-panel-verdict.md:22, 57, 96-104
  • Docs have no external verifier; reading is their only check (RF-3). The Theory Ledger that P10 invokes was ranked #2 but never shipped and never measured, and its 'independent verifier re-derives periodically' is the same unanswered question P10 now inherits. docs/features/2026-07-20-reading-fatigue-panel/research.md:31, 41-43
  • Team setup records per-area owners but nothing ties a correction to an owner or forces re-approval when implementer differs from corrector. src/skills/joycraft-collaborative-setup.md:44-82

Evidence against it

  • Decisions invisible in code do exist and curated decision context measurably raises compliance on them (+49pp). If the architecture-defense session is scoped to record only what code cannot show (rejected alternatives, rationale, off-repo constraints), DCBench supports it. arXiv 2605.08112, live fetch 2026-09-24
  • Fresh-context verifier subagents outperform self-critique, so a verifier that re-derives the record against code is a vendor-endorsed mechanism, and the record could serve as that verifier's oracle. platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/prompting-claude-fable-5.md, 'Recommended scaffolding changes', live fetch 2026-09-24
  • Deterministic architecture-conformance checks exist as CI tooling (dependency rules that fail the build), so the 'what re-checks corrections as code drifts' question has a known answer for the structural subset. https://github.com/sverweij/dependency-cruiser README, live fetch 2026-09-24
  • Joycraft's own escalation rule already says a fact enforceable as architecture, a deny pattern, or a CI check goes to harden, not prose. P10 has a legitimate home if its outputs are routed through that rule. src/skills/joycraft-add-fact.md:24; src/skills/joycraft-session-end.md:64
  • All six prior panelists kept the decision log, and the design skill demonstrably reused five prior rows to constrain its own choices in-session. docs/research/2026-09-01-context-map-panel-verdict.md:20-22

On the human's position

Section 10 has no direct P10 answer; the maintainer's relevant words are Q4 ("in recent sessions I've been getting some slop that took hours and that was not shippable, we have to close that gap") and Q1 ("Gates + lifecycle + artifacts fixed; process prose generated"), plus the §0 origin ("much less slop, especially the 'slop on slop' that accretes as a project matures"; "it requires a CS background"). My lens moves the Q4 framing hard: the slop the maintainer describes appears inside the implement loop, and nothing on that path reads an architecture record today (verify.md:34-42, 100; implement reads no docs/context). A record written at setup or at a maturity gate cannot close a gap on a path that never opens it. Q1 actually argues against P10 as proposed: if gates are the invariant and prose is disposable, then an architecture record only earns a place when each correction terminates as a gate (a dependency rule, deny pattern, or CI check via harden) or as a decision-log row that verify's oracle is extended to read. The "CS background" constraint the maintainer accepted is also a confound: a practitioner who corrects an agent's architecture at setup would plausibly produce less slop with or without the record, and the colleague's report cannot separate the two. On "setup step": for a greenfield project there is no code to defend with code examples, so the setup instance reduces to design Section 3-4 (src/skills/joycraft-design.md:95-105), which already exists. The maintainer's frame survives only as a maturity gate whose output is checks, piloted with a before/after count of verify FINDINGS or a DCBench-style compliance probe on the project's own corrections.

Evidence auditorqualified
Strongest refutation

P10's word "enforceable" has no citation behind it and no mechanism in the repo. Helix (shopify.engineering/helix, fetched 2026-09-24) says "This documentation makes adversarial review enforceable" — but the documentation there is an architecture the engineers wrote up front, and enforcement is "Two independent, context-isolated reviewer agents check the new code against it." The page does not say that engineer corrections become a document, nor how "memory" is stored (the pack's own "Not stated" caveat, §0 line 20, is correct). So Helix supports "reviewers check code against a written architecture," not "human corrections accrete into a record." The second pillar, the Theory Ledger, is a proposal citing a proposal: no docs/context/theory.md or template exists, and the brief hedges it as "arguably the strongest single idea" (docs/research/2026-07-20-reading-fatigue-brief.html:370) — the pack drops "arguably". The third pillar is one colleague's unquantified anecdote (§0 line 22). Meanwhile the one controlled study in the pack cuts against a read-on-demand record: Gloaguen et al. v2 (arXiv 2602.11988, 2026-06-23) finds context files, "both LLM-generated and developer-committed," "do not generally improve task success rates, while increasing inference cost by over 20% on average," and "repository overviews ... are not helpful." In the repo today nothing re-checks the corrections as code drifts: verify's oracle is the brief's Hard Constraints, its decisions: frontmatter, and AGENTS.md boundaries (src/skills/joycraft-verify.md:38-42) — not decision-log.md or dangerous-assumptions.md; harden can only enforce rules statable "as a command regex or file-path pattern" (src/skills/joycraft-harden.md:35-37) and names permissions.deny plus deny-patterns.txt as "the only two enforcement surfaces" (harden.md:20); no skill acts on the decision log's "Revisit When" column (only decide.md:255 writes it). An architecture record written today would be hopeful disclosure by the context-map panel's own definition (2026-09-01 verdict line 57): the Context Map has one row (AGENTS.md:189-191).

Qualification

P10 stands only under all of: (1) the record is consumed as an oracle by an independent verifier (verify Step 2.5 and any Helix-style reviewer gate) and re-derived from code by a fresh-context subagent on a schedule, with diffs surfaced — not merely written to docs/context and pointed at from the Context Map; (2) it is a maturity gate for the practitioner path, not a universal setup step, because gather-context.md:27 forbids the code scan by default and the pack itself says the practice needs a CS background; (3) 'enforceable' is limited to what a verifier can check — architecture rules cannot become deny patterns (harden.md:35-37); (4) the Theory Ledger and the colleague's report are labeled as untested proposals, not evidence, until a with/without run exists.

This documentation makes adversarial review enforceable." / "Two independent, context-isolated reviewer agents check the new code against it" / "Helix records it in memory to improve every checkpoint that follows"; storage not specified.
  • Context files, whether LLM-generated or developer-committed, do not generally improve task success and add >20% inference cost; repository overviews are not helpful. https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.11988 (Gloaguen, Mündler, Müller, Raychev, Vechev; v1 2026-02-12, v2 2026-06-23), abstract, fetched 2026-09-24.

On the human's position

Section 10 has no direct answer on P10; the nearest are Q4 and the §0 anecdote. Q4: "we are already doing alot of what helix is doing, but I think what they do better is that once they actually get tot he implementation loop it's basically sit back and relax and have full confidence... we have to close that gap." Taken at its word, the maintainer's own diagnosis argues against P10 as framed: the Helix mechanism that produces that confidence is two isolated reviewers checking code against a written architecture plus blocking gates — a verifier-side change — not a setup-time defense session whose output is a document. Joycraft already has the reviewer half's skeleton (verify.md:34-42 feeds stamped decisions to a fresh subagent); what it lacks is the architecture doc as an oracle input and a re-derivation pass. The §0 framing ("corrections become a core part of the context map") is the weakest version: the context map is hopeful disclosure with one row, and Gloaguen's controlled result says read-on-demand context files do not lift task success. My lens moves the position this far: P10 survives only if 'enforceable architecture record' is operationalized as a verifier oracle (an input to verify and to Helix-style reviewers, with a periodic independent re-derivation diffed against code, as the Theory Ledger proposed), never as a context-map pointer. As a setup step it also collides with gather-context.md:27's explicit no-code-scan cost rule and with the constraint the maintainer himself recorded — 'requires a CS background, so it is useless for Joycraft's novice users' — so it is a practitioner-tier maturity gate at most, and the Q2 'one path' answer needs a fork to accommodate it.

P11 · 4 skeptics

A user technical-background profile forks the abstraction level

flip
Ruling

P11 does not stand. A setup-time technical-background profile that forks which gates run, how much ceremony applies, and what artifacts show contradicts the maintainer's own Q1 invariant (gates + lifecycle + artifacts fixed) and Q2 (one path), has no per-user home in Joycraft's file model without breaking committed team artifacts, rests on a single unmeasured anecdote from a non-user, and its only shipped precedent (BMAD `user_skill_level`) was removed on 2026-08-09. Replace with: altitude is a per-project property set once by the repo owner next to the Execution Profile in AGENTS.md; the only per-user residue is an uncommitted explanation-depth preference that changes presentation, never gates, ceremony, or committed content.

The claim as argued

Setup captures the user's technical background and forks vocabulary, which gates run, how much ceremony, and what artifacts show, so novices and practitioners walk one path at different altitudes. Skeptic angles: self-assessed skill is unreliable and drifts (infer from behavior instead?); does the fork change content or only vocabulary; is the novice path Joycraft's market at all; a per-user fork conflicts with committed shared artifacts on a team; the execution profile in AGENTS.md is per-harness, not per-user.

Replacement claim

Altitude belongs to the project, not the person. Whoever owns the repo sets it once, in AGENTS.md beside the Execution Profile, identical for every author; gates, ceremony, checkpoint questions, specs, decision rows, and PR bodies are one path per project. The P10 architecture-defense gate runs for everyone; the agent carries the CS load by explaining each decision in STE, it does not skip the gate for anyone. The one per-user knob is an uncommitted, revocable explanation-depth preference living in docs/.joycraft/local/ (or the host's per-user output style on Claude Code), inside the STE contract (plainer sentences, not a second vocabulary), that changes how results are explained and nothing else. Build even that only after one named daily user who cannot read a diff exists, and instrument the brief's existing unread `User expertise` field first to see whether it ever changes an outcome.

Condition

The residue (per-user explanation depth) holds only if all four are true: (1) it is stored uncommitted (docs/.joycraft/local/ or .claude/settings.local.json), (2) it changes no gate, no ceremony count, and no committed artifact, (3) it stays inside the STE output contract rather than forking vocabulary, and (4) a named user who needs it is using Joycraft daily. If the profile gates any gate or writes to any committed file, the proposition is refuted for any project with more than one author.

Judge's reasoning

Four independent grounds, each sufficient. (1) Frame contradiction: the maintainer fixed "Gates + lifecycle + artifacts" as the invariant (§10 Q1) and confirmed "one path" (§10 Q2) with the prediction that skill spread "becomes a non issue" as the harness drives more. P11's fork of "which gates run, how much ceremony, what the artifacts show" varies exactly what Q1 fixes; strip that and only vocabulary remains, which frontier models adapt per reader without a stored profile and which the STE contract (src/templates/reference/output-style.md, rule 10: one word for one concept) already fixes for everyone. (2) No home: the Execution Profile is "team-shared data the human owns and hand-edits", per-harness, ONE_HOME (src/execution-profile.ts:9-11); AGENTS.md is create-once and never regenerated (src/update-inventory.ts:228-261); the manifest has only vendor|create-once|config-patch kinds (src/install-manifest.ts:30); the sole gitignored per-user home is docs/.joycraft/local/ (.gitignore:15), which today holds one presentation flag (autoOpen, joycraft-tune.md:89). A profile that changes committed artifacts therefore either lives in a shared file (every author gets the same altitude, so it is a project setting) or needs new machinery for an unproven need. (3) No demand signal: the brief template has carried `User expertise: [comfortable / learning / needs guidance]` (src/skills/joycraft-new-feature.md:181) and nothing in src/skills, src/*.ts, src/templates, or tests consumes it (verified grep: only the template line and its generated bundle copies). The pack's positive case is one secondhand practice from a colleague who does not use Joycraft (§0), and no named Joycraft user cannot read a diff. (4) Precedent and measurement point the other way: BMAD removed `user_skill_level` tailoring in v6.11.0 (verified live, CHANGELOG line under "## v6.11.0 - 2026-08-09"); the Bing Copilot study (arXiv 2502.18685) found expert-register responses correlate with positive UX regardless of user level while under-pitching hurts; arXiv 2608.10319 found pooled generic skills beat per-developer personalized ones; every "adapt to capability" result in the pack (§4.4, §4.5) is about backbone model tier with no human variable. The self-assessment-reliability angle is weaker than the pack implies (Feigenspan ρ=0.539 for a single programming-experience question; McIntosh r=0.43-0.47 in general) and I do not rest the ruling on it; the drift problem is real though, since the product's stated job is to move the user up levels and no mechanism re-scores a setup snapshot. The team-lead's "qualified" and the three "refuted" verdicts converge on the same residue, and that residue is not "forks the abstraction level"; it is a verbosity preference. Hence flip, with the replacement claim naming where altitude actually lives.

Strongest refutation considered

The strongest case FOR P11: the maintainer explicitly asked for a novice-vibe-coder lens (Q7) and describes his fifteen colleagues as "mixed skill"; the P10 architecture-defense practice is reported to need a CS background, so some user-keyed gating of P10 answers a real need; a per-user, per-project gitignored home already exists (docs/.joycraft/local/, and Claude Code's settings.local.json is documented as "personal exceptions don't need a commit"); programmer self-estimate correlates ρ=0.539 with measured comprehension, so the input is not useless; and expertise alignment does matter in one direction (arXiv 2502.18685: pitching below an expert hurts). I weighed this and it does not rescue P11 as written: it supports a per-user presentation preference, not a fork of gates or artifacts, and the P10 need is better met by explaining the defense at the reader's level than by skipping it, since skipping it makes the gate advisory by author, which Q4 ("gates that cannot be overridden") rejects. The self-estimate correlation is also about static programming experience, not the AI-assisted level that the product intends to change.

Human position moved?

Yes, moved, and in the direction of the human's own words. Section 10 has no direct P11 answer; the fork is the human's proposed mechanism in §0 ("setup asks for the user's technical background, and that forks the abstraction level"), framed to serve the Atharva architecture-defense practice for practitioners while sparing 'novice users'. The panel moves that position on four points of evidence. First, the human's Q1 ("Gates + lifecycle + artifacts fixed; process prose generated") and Q2 ("one path"; "as this system gets ... more driven by the harness this becomes a non issue") already contradict the mechanism: a fork of gates and artifacts by user is what Q1 fixes, and 'one path' is the opposite of two altitudes. Second, the novice segment is asserted, not shown: no named user cannot read a diff, Joycraft's own levels guide targets Levels 3-4, and the Shapiro framework cited for 'novice' has no non-programmer tier. Third, the repo has run the experiment quietly: the brief's `User expertise` field has existed with zero consumers, and the only shipped precedent (BMAD) dropped its tailoring six weeks ago. Fourth, the measured data (Bing Copilot: expert register is fine regardless of user level; arXiv 2608.10319: pooled beats personalized) says the practitioner altitude should be the default for everyone. Where the human lands after the panel: keep P10 as a gate for all users and let the agent do the explaining in STE; set any altitude per project in AGENTS.md next to the Execution Profile; treat per-user explanation depth as an uncommitted rendering preference, built only when a named user needs it; and pursue 'teach people' through content and a simpler harness, as the human himself predicted, not through a setup question.

Skeptic disagreements

  • Verdict split: team-lead ruled 'qualified', novice, ai-researcher and evidence-auditor ruled 'refuted'. Their qualifications converge on the same residue (per-user, uncommitted, presentation-only), so the split is over whether that residue counts as P11 surviving.
  • Self-assessment reliability: team-lead says weak (McIntosh et al. 2022, r=0.43-0.47) and evidence-auditor adds novices misjudge quality (Cloude et al. LAK 2024); evidence-auditor and novice counter that a single programming-experience self-estimate correlates well (Feigenspan et al. 2012, rho=0.539; Siegmund et al.) and that the pack's 'unreliable' angle is overstated. Novice explicitly says its refutation does not rest on this point.
  • Where the residue lives: team-lead wants it in Joycraft's docs/.joycraft/local/ (cross-harness, Joycraft-owned); evidence-auditor says Claude Code output styles in .claude/settings.local.json already ship it and Joycraft should contribute only a pointer (Claude-only; no verified equivalent on Codex/Pi/omp/Copilot); ai-researcher wants a BMAD-style config.user.toml value shipped only behind a measured delta; novice wants no stored profile at all and per-session inference from how the human talks, with the unread 'User expertise' brief line as the home.
  • Infer-from-behavior: novice's qualification endorses per-session inference; team-lead and ai-researcher reject behavior inference (arXiv 2608.10319: pooled generic skills beat personalized; joycraft-optimize.md:70: per-machine counts stop being evidence past ~3 contributors); evidence-auditor found no source either way and notes joycraft telemetry records reads, not skill signals.
  • Whether a vocabulary fork is worth anything: ai-researcher reads arXiv 2502.18685 as showing the expert register is fine regardless of user level, cutting against even a vocabulary residue; team-lead and evidence-auditor treat plainer explanation as a legitimate rendering preference; team-lead adds that a vocabulary fork on shared artifacts violates STE rule 10.
  • Shapiro citation label: novice marks it 'holds' with a note that the novice/no-CS framing extends past the source; team-lead and evidence-auditor mark it 'misread'. Same substance, different label.
  • Whether a mixed-skill audience exists: all four say unverified; novice and evidence-auditor treat Q2's 'mixed skill' as asserted not shown; team-lead and ai-researcher grant Q7's novice lens as some pull toward P11.
  • Which mechanism absorbs the skill gap: novice and evidence-auditor read the maintainer's 'becomes a non issue' as the harness doing more; team-lead says the default altitude should be the super-user's set per project; ai-researcher says treat any fork as an eval question (delta on held-out tasks) not a setup question.

Citation problems

  • Dan Shapiro 'Five Levels' (pack §0, §9 P11; docs/guides/levels.md): misread. The post's levels are collaboration modes for developers; it has no non-programmer tier, so 'novice ... no CS background = Levels 1-2' is the pack's gloss. levels.md:17 'Most developers plateau at Level 2' also does not match the source, which puts '90% of AI-native developers' at Level 2 and says 'almost everyone tops out' at Level 3.
  • Skill-creator post (pack §4.6): the implied URL claude.com/blog/skill-creator returns 404; live page is claude.com/blog/improving-skill-creator-test-measure-and-refine-agent-skills (2026-03-03). Live wording is softer: 'may become less necessary as models improve' and encoded-preference skills are 'more durable', not 'persist'; preferences are framed as 'your team's process', not per-user.
  • gstack (pack §5.5): the setup profile is per-MODEL (reads Codex config.toml), not per-user, and the README tells the user to add the 'Skill routing' CLAUDE.md section manually rather than setup writing it (evidence-auditor, fetched live).
  • McIntosh et al. 2022 at royalsocietypublishing.org: HTTP 403 (dead for the panel); verified via PMC mirror PMC9727674.
  • Pack §8.6 '10 of 22 skills exceed 200 lines': 12 by optimize's own wc -l method (evidence-auditor). Not P11-specific but a pack error.
  • SkillsBench (pack §4.1) cites the superseded v1 (+16.2pp, 86 tasks); current revision (2026-06-14) reports 87 tasks, +16.6pp, and the abstract no longer mentions the self-generated condition (ai-researcher).
  • Pack §4 inference 'per-user regeneration risks the ACE-style collapse' extends an online-adaptation-without-feedback result to static profiles; that step is the pack's, not the paper's (evidence-auditor).
  • Anthropic 'How AI assistance impacts the formation of coding skills' (2026-01-29, 52 devs, -17%): numbers from secondary search hits only; primary not fetched by any skeptic.
  • Feigenspan et al. 2012 rho=0.539 and Cloude et al. LAK 2024: secondary snippets only; Springer redirected to auth, ACM returned 403.
  • Atharva Vaidya architecture-defense practice and its 'requires a CS background' constraint (pack §0): personal report, no URL, no artifact; the entire positive case for P11 rests on it.

What would change the ruling

Any one of: (1) a named daily Joycraft user who cannot read a diff, with a specific gate where they churn or abandon, which would make the novice path a real segment rather than an asserted one; (2) instrumenting the existing `User expertise` brief field and showing that its value changes any downstream outcome (gate pass rate, rework, abandonment) across several features; (3) a measured delta on a held-out task set (per `claude plugin eval` or Joycraft's own evals) showing that a self-declared altitude improves shippability or reduces abandonment versus one path with STE explanation; (4) evidence that the P10 architecture-defense gate fails for non-CS users even when explained at their level, rather than being merely uncomfortable, which would justify user-keyed gating of P10 specifically; (5) a per-user, uncommitted instruction surface appearing on Codex, Pi, omp, or Copilot, which would make a cross-harness per-user profile implementable without new Joycraft machinery. Evidence that self-assessment is more reliable than the pack implies would NOT change the ruling, because the ruling rests on the frame contradiction, the missing home, and the absent demand, not on unreliability.

Skeptics

Novice vibe coderrefuted
Strongest refutation

The proposition adds the one thing that makes me quit — another setup question I cannot answer — to serve a user who does not exist in the confirmed frame. Shapiro's Levels 1–2 are developers ("You're writing the important stuff, but you offload specific, discrete tasks to your AI intern"; "pairing with the AI like a colleague"); the post has no non-programmer tier, so "no CS background" and "Level 1–2" are two different axes that §0 line 22 conflates. Joycraft's own levels.md:22-23 says its job is Levels 3–4; the README (line 45) starts me at `npm install -g joycraft` and (line 160) tells me "you approve the brief and the specs, the agent executes with TDD". The maintainer's Q2 names the users: himself and ~15 daily-driver colleagues on "one path". Nobody named cannot read a diff. Meanwhile today's setup already asks me which harnesses (`claude, codex, pi, copilot, omp` — harness.ts:78-84), then four execution-profile questions per harness ("Use swarms for decompose?", "Model", "Effort" — execution-profile.ts:173-188), then shared/private git tracking, then auto-memory (setup-walkthrough.md:36-45); tune adds 3–5 risk questions plus git autonomy (tuning.md:9,20); new-feature asks "smoke test budget? lockdown mode desired?" (new-feature.md:104). A "what is your technical background?" question is one more I will answer wrong ("intermediate, I shipped an app with Cursor"), and because the fork "gates which gates run", my wrong answer silently changes what I get with no way for me to notice. Joycraft already captured this exact self-assessment once — the brief template's "**User expertise:** [comfortable / learning / needs guidance]" (new-feature.md:181) — and zero skills, templates, or tests read it (grep of src/skills, src/templates, tests: one hit, the template line). The demand for a fork never materialized in the product's own skills. And because Q1 fixes gates, lifecycle, artifacts, STE and the TDD loop as invariant, the only thing left for my "altitude" to change is vocabulary and hiding the P10 code-defense gate — vocabulary the model already adapts per reader without a stored profile (Fable 5 guide: "The vocabulary you built up while working is yours, not theirs; leave it behind"). Finally, the product's promise is to move me from Level 1 to Level 4; a background snapshot taken at setup is wrong within weeks if the product works, and unlike tune (re-scored every run) nothing re-scores it.

Qualification

Not P11, but what could survive from it: no setup question and no stored profile; the agent infers reader mode per session from how the human talks (the existing unread 'User expertise' line is the natural home) and changes presentation only — which evidence an artifact shows (screenshot vs diff), never which gates run or how many. Even that is worth building only after one named user who cannot read a diff is using Joycraft daily.

On the human's position

Section 10 has no direct P11 answer; the nearest positions are Q2 and Q1. Q2: \"Me truly first as I am the super user of this product, but I now have about 15 colleagues all of use it daily driver ... if I can get it to work best for me, we can easily get it for others especially then I'll make content etc.. around into teach people, but the hope also being that as this system gets much easier house and more driven by the harness this becomes a non issue really\" — confirmed as \"one path\". Q1: \"getting people used to TDD agentic development as opposed to endless vibe coding (the essence and core objective of joycraft)\". My lens moves both toward my verdict, hard. First, the maintainer's own words already contain the alternative to a fork: 'one path', 'make content ... to teach people', and 'as this system gets ... more driven by the harness this becomes a non issue'. That is the harness absorbing the skill difference, not branching on it. Second, Q1 says the objective is to move me up to TDD; a background captured at setup pins me at the altitude I started at, and nothing re-scores it (AGENTS.md is create-once, update-inventory.ts:228-261). The fork contradicts the core objective. Third, the attack: 'mixed skill' is asserted, not shown. The maintainer is the super-user; the colleagues are engineers on teams; the one person with the architecture-defense practice does not use Joycraft. Until one real user who cannot read a diff is named, the novice altitude is a path the maintainer will never walk, and this repo already shows what happens to unwalked paths (folder map never regenerated, §8.4; 'User expertise' field never read, new-feature.md:181). What would keep me in week two is fewer unanswerable questions and decisions I can make by looking (P9's visuals) — neither needs a profile, and the first is made worse by one.

Team lead, five engineersqualified
Strongest refutation

On a team, "altitude" is a property of the project, not the person. Every artifact the fork would change is committed and shared: AGENTS.md and the Execution Profile are create-once, team-owned, ONE_HOME data (src/update-inventory.ts:233-262; src/execution-profile.ts:9-12 "team-shared data the human owns"), docs/.joycraft/manifest.json is tracked (git ls-files), and checkpoint pages, decision rows, and specs land in the repo. If a per-user profile gates which gates run (P9 visuals vs P10 code-level defense) or how much ceremony applies, then the same repo accumulates features that passed different gates depending on who typed the prompt. The lead cannot assume any feature passed the architecture defense, review load rises because artifact shape varies by author, and the decision log becomes inconsistent by author. That is an advisory gate by another name, which the maintainer's own Q4 answer ("gates that cannot be overridden") and Helix ("gates are blocking, never advisory", pack §0) both reject. The input to the fork is also weak: self-estimates track measured ability at r = 0.43-0.47 (McIntosh et al., Royal Society Open Science 2022, n=151), and the one empirical study of per-developer personalization found "small and inconsistent improvements" versus "the largest and most consistent gains" from generic skills pooled across developers (arXiv 2608.10319, 2026-08-10, 206 sessions, 13 developers). Anthropic's skill-creator post frames encoded-preference skills as sequencing "according to your team's process", not the individual's (claude.com, 2026-03-03). Finally the vocabulary half collides with the maintainer's Q1 invariant: the STE output contract governs all human-facing output and rule 10 says "one word for one concept" (src/templates/reference/output-style.md:6-9 and rule 10); STE in pragmatic mode is already the single-register answer for readers of mixed ability, so a per-user vocabulary fork forks the invariant. There is no cross-harness per-user home either: CLAUDE.local.md counts as a CLAUDE.md and stops AGENTS.md loading on Claude Code (code.claude.com/docs/en/memory, table rows for AGENTS.md; fetched 2026-09-24), Codex reads AGENTS.md with no per-user project instruction layer (pack §3 table), and Joycraft's only gitignored per-user-per-project home is docs/.joycraft/local/ (.gitignore:15), which today holds one presentation flag, autoOpen (src/skills/joycraft-tune.md:89).

Qualification

P11 survives only as a per-user rendering preference: vocabulary and explanation depth in chat and in the human-facing parts of artifacts, stored per user and gitignored under docs/.joycraft/local/, overridable per session, and inside the STE contract (plainer sentences, not a second term set). Under that condition the fork changes nothing that is committed: which gates run, how much ceremony applies, what a checkpoint asks, and what lands in specs, decision rows, and PR bodies stay identical for every author and are set per project in AGENTS.md by the repo owner. If the profile gates any gate or ceremony, or if it writes into any committed artifact, the proposition is refuted for any project with more than one author.

On the human's position

The maintainer's Q2 answer is "Solo practitioners of mixed skill; maintainer first as super-user, colleagues second, one path", and the rationale adds that the colleagues are "across different size teams" and that "as this system gets much easier ... more driven by the harness this becomes a non issue really." Two of the maintainer's own words refute P11 as written. "One path" is the opposite of a per-user fork of gates and ceremony. And "this becomes a non issue" is an argument that the skill gap is closed by the harness doing more, not by asking the user how skilled they are. The Q1 rationale names STE a "biggest win": STE exists so that one register serves a tired or inexperienced reader and an expert alike, and its rule 10 forbids rotating vocabulary within a document, so a per-user vocabulary fork on shared artifacts contradicts the invariant the maintainer wants fixed. My lens moves the position in one direction only: harder toward one path. The altitude must be set per project by whoever owns the repo (the lead), in the committed AGENTS.md next to the Execution Profile, identical for every author; the default altitude is the super-user's, because that is who the product is tuned for. What a novice on the team gets is not fewer gates but the same gates with plainer explanation in the human channel, and that is a rendering preference that belongs in docs/.joycraft/local/, never a gate switch. The maintainer's design should also reject "infer from behavior": the one study on it found generic pooled skills beat personalized ones, and the repo's own optimize skill already documents that per-machine behavioral counts stop being evidence past three contributors.

AI researcherrefuted
Strongest refutation

P11 has no measurement behind it and borrows its plausibility from studies about a different variable. Every "adapt to capability" result in the pack — the harness ablation (planning +11.6pp for Nemotron-3 30B, −2.0/−0.4pp for 550B and Mistral-Medium at ~30% lower cost) and Lin et al.'s inverted-U — measures the agent's pass rate as a function of the backbone MODEL with no human in the loop; transferring that to human expertise is a category error. The one measurement that does concern user expertise (Bing Copilot, 25k conversations, arXiv 2502.18685) found the agent answering at proficient/expert level "correlates with positive user experience regardless of the user's level of expertise," while answering BELOW the user's level hurts, most on complex tasks — so the fork's only reachable failure (a practitioner routed down to the novice altitude) is the measured harm, and the "benefit" (a novice routed down) is a direction the data says is unnecessary. The gate input itself is unreliable in exactly this population: METR's RCT (16 experienced devs, 246 issues, 2025-07-10) had developers predict +24%, measure −19%, and still believe +20% afterward; Anthropic's 52-developer RCT (2026-01-29) shows the novice who would most need the fork is the one whose comprehension is being eroded by delegation, i.e. the level drifts under the tool. The only harness that shipped this exact knob — BMAD's `user_skill_level` (beginner/intermediate/expert, per-user config) — removed it from its Build skill in v6.11.0 on 2026-08-09 ("Build drops its `user_name` greeting and `user_skill_level` tailoring"). And Joycraft has quietly run this experiment already: the brief template captures `User expertise: [comfortable / learning / needs guidance]` (src/skills/joycraft-new-feature.md:181) and nothing in src/skills, src/*.ts, templates, or tests consumes it — a self-declared expertise field with zero downstream effect and zero telemetry. Finally, the proposition contradicts the human's own frame: Q1 fixes "Gates + lifecycle + artifacts" as the invariant, and P11 varies which gates run and what artifacts show per user.

Qualification

Survives only as a per-user, uncommitted, revocable explanation-depth preference that changes no gate, no artifact, and no committed file — i.e. BMAD's pre-v6.11 `user_skill_level` in config.user.toml — and only if it is shipped behind a measured Δ on a held-out task set. That is not "forks the abstraction level"; it is a verbosity setting the only precedent already dropped.

On the human's position

Section 10 never states a position on P11 directly; the fork is the lead's mechanism for the maintainer's Atharva observation in §0 ("requires a CS background, so it is useless for Joycraft's novice users"). The maintainer's own words cut against P11 twice. Q1: the invariant is "Gates + lifecycle + artifacts fixed; process prose generated" — P11 varies which gates run (P9 visuals vs P10 code defense) and what artifacts show, so it forks the very thing Q1 declares invariant; if only prose varies, the proposition collapses to vocabulary, which frontier models already adapt without a profile and which the Bing data says is fine at the expert register. Q2: "Me truly first as I am the super user... then I'll make content etc.. around into teach people... as this system gets much easier house and more driven by the harness this becomes a non issue really" — one path, maintainer first, novices served by content and by the harness getting simpler, not by a second altitude. The only pull toward P11 is Q7's added novice-vibe-coder lens. My lens moves the human's position by removing a false premise: the maintainer treats a background question as a reliable input, and the one population measured (experienced developers, METR) mis-assesses by ~39pp even after direct experience. The measured, cheap replacement is behavioral: Joycraft already has `joycraft telemetry` and the unread `User expertise` field; instrument whether that field ever changes an outcome before building a fork on it. Concretely: keep gates and artifacts one path, let the agent explain more when asked, and treat any per-user fork as an eval question (Δ on a held-out task set, à la `claude plugin eval`) rather than a setup question.

Evidence auditorrefuted
Strongest refutation

P11 has no evidence base. Its only support in the pack is one uncited anecdote from a colleague who does not use Joycraft (evidence pack §0, "Architecture-defense session"); none of the nine external sources I re-fetched shows any harness forking on a user's self-declared technical background — gstack forks per MODEL (reads config.toml, github.com/garrytan/gstack README, fetched 2026-09-24), Helix adapts per accumulated approved work and "makes no mention" of engineer skill or per-user profiles (shopify.engineering/helix, 2026-09-21), and Anthropic's skill-creator post ties durable skills to "your team's process," not to individuals (claude.com/blog/improving-skill-creator, 2026-03-03). The one framework P11 uses to define "novice" is misread: Dan Shapiro's levels are collaboration modes, not skill levels; the post puts "90% of 'AI-native' developers" at Level 2 and says "almost everyone tops out" at Level 3 (danshapiro.com, 2026-01-23), so "Levels 1-2 = novice market" is not in the source (Joycraft's own docs/guides/levels.md:17 says "Most developers plateau at Level 2," which also does not match the source). The fork P11 wants — "which gates run, how much ceremony, and what artifacts show" — is exactly what the human fixed as the invariant in Q1 ("Gates + lifecycle + artifacts fixed; process prose generated"), and the vocabulary residue already exists per-user outside Joycraft: Claude Code output styles (Explanatory: "You're getting to know a codebase"; Learning: hands-on practice) stored in .claude/settings.local.json, which Claude Code keeps out of git (code.claude.com/docs/en/output-styles and /settings, fetched 2026-09-24). What is left for Joycraft to build is either already shipped by the host or contradicts the human's own invariant.

Qualification

The only residue that survives: a per-user, non-committed vocabulary/explanation setting (Claude Code output style or an equivalent in .claude/settings.local.json) that changes how results are explained and never which gates run, how much ceremony, or what artifacts contain. That residue is already shipped by Claude Code and has no verified equivalent on Codex, Pi, omp, or Copilot, so Joycraft's contribution would be a one-line pointer, not a profile captured at setup.

On the human's position

The human's Q2 words: "Me truly first as I am the super user of this product… 15 colleagues all of use it daily driver, across different size teams… if I can get it to work best for me, we can easily get it for others… as this system gets much easier house and more driven by the harness this becomes a non issue really" — confirmed as "maintainer first as the super-user, colleagues second, ONE path." And Q1: "Gates + lifecycle + artifacts fixed; process prose generated," naming STE as a "biggest win." Read literally, the human has already voted against P11 twice: one path, not two altitudes; gates and artifacts fixed, not forked by user; and STE (docs/templates/reference/output-style.md, vendor-owned) already fixes the human-facing vocabulary for everyone, which is the exact thing a vocabulary fork would vary. The human's own prediction — that the novice/practitioner gap "becomes a non issue" once the harness drives more — is the strongest argument against building a background profile now, and it needs no evidence I could not find. My lens moves the position in one direction only: it strengthens it. The human's "mixed skill" audience claim is unverified (no data on the fifteen colleagues), the framework Joycraft cites for novice-vs-practitioner is misread at the source, and the only per-user altitude mechanism verified live (Claude Code output styles, per-user, gitignored) already exists outside Joycraft. If the maintainer still wants an altitude knob, the evidence supports at most: point users at the host's per-user output style, and never let any per-user setting change which gates run.

Evidence pack audit

Every item below is a place where the evidence pack (the lead's document) misread, misattributed, or overstated a source, as found by the skeptics and judges re-fetching it. The Codex panel should re-check these too.
